Regarding the term "heart" (*hṛt*): the connection is that one should place [the syllables] starting from the heart upon the hands, feet, flanks, and mouth.

By this, it is stated that [the placement occurs] on the heart and so forth of the two hands, on the heart and so forth of the two feet, on the heart and so forth of the flank, and on the heart and so forth of the mouth.

163–164 | "In this very way" means: according to the sequence already described, the collection of fifty letters (*pañcāśad-varṇa-sañcaya*)—enclosed by the *praṇava* (the syllable *oṃ*) at the beginning and end, or ending with *namaḥ*; joined with the *bindu*, or devoid of the *bindu*; with the *visarga* at the end, or accompanied by both the *bindu* and the *visarga*—should be deposited. Regarding the fruit of depositing the letters with the aforementioned *bindu* at the beginning and end, he says:
"Rahasyam," etc., is clear. 165–166.

Regarding "māyā": in this ritual placement (*nyāsa*), when it is impossible to perform the placements with the aforementioned fingers, one should perform the *bījayāga* (seed-sacrifice) of the letters of the alphabet beginning with 'a' as previously described. (Page 473)
One may perform the ritual placements (nyāsa) either mentally, or with flowers, or even by means of a healthy [hand];
or one may perform them in all rites through the joining of the thumb and the ring finger.
In this very manner, one should perform the ritual placement of the phonemes (varṇanyāsa).
(Sūryādidevatāpūjā) One should first worship the Sun, Gaṇeśa, and Viṣṇu as the presiding deity;
thereafter, one should perform the worship of Śiva according to the prescribed rule with their respective mantras. (167)
(Hand-assignment [karaṇyāsa]:
One should perform the purification of the hands with the *vidyā* that purifies the hands, repeating it twice over the fingers from the middle finger to the palms. (168)

He describes the fourfold ritual (*kalpa*) with the words beginning with "māyā" and so forth. In that regard, one method is that the placement (*nyāsa*) should be performed by first joining the seed-syllables of Māyā and Ramā, namely *hrīṃ* and *śrīṃ*. Another is that the collection of fifty letters should be placed preceded by the seed-syllable of Vāgbhava, namely *aiṃ*. Yet another is that it is preceded by the triad, meaning it is preceded by the three aforementioned seed-syllables characterized as Māyā, Lakṣmī, and Vāgbhava. [And] "preceded by Ramā" means...

The word "Śrī" is the first [mantra] beginning with the seed-syllable of Lakṣmī (śrīṃ); the other is as follows: by joining the seed-syllables according to the previously stated sequence to mantras such as "aṃ namaḥ" and "āṃ namaḥ," the resulting application culminates in forms such as "hrīṃ śrīṃ āṃ namaḥ," or "aiṃ āṃ namaḥ," or "hrīṃ śrīṃ aiṃ āṃ namaḥ," or "śrīṃ āṃ namaḥ. In this regard:

Because of the separate mention of "ramādya" (beginning with *ra*), it should be understood that in the phrase "preceded by the seeds of Māyā and Lakṣmī," there is a simultaneous application of both Māyā and Lakṣmī. By the term "kramāt" (in sequence), the reversal of the order of the seed-syllables is prohibited.
Regarding what must be done when the placement (*nyāsa*) on the respective fingers in the previously mentioned form is impossible, he says "with the mind," and so forth.
This is clear.

167. Now, he describes the worship of the Sun and the others with the verse beginning "the Sun," etc. The meaning is that one should worship the Sun, Gaṇeśa, Viṣṇu, and Śiva in sequence. "With their respective mantras" means with those mantras prescribed in the ritual manuals (kalpas) for each of those deities.
Or [one may perform it] with [mantras] beginning with *praṇava* and ending with *namaḥ*.
168. He describes the ritual placement on the hands (*karanyāsa*) with the words "purification of the hands" (*karaśuddhi*), etc. This sequence has already been demonstrated previously.
(The ritual placement of the six seats: *ṣaḍāsananyāsa*).
Then the best of practitioners should perform the placement of the six seats (ṣaḍāsananyāsa):
with the mantra "O Tripureśī," he should place the seat of nectar (amṛtāsana) upon the two feet. 169.
Having uttered the *kumārikā*, one should then utter *Tripurasundarī*;
[one should place] the lotus-throne of the child upon the two knees, and abandon the *bālā* and the rest.

There, having superimposed Māyā, [one places] "Tripuravāsinī" on the seat of the Self (ātma-āsana) upon the pair of thighs; then, on the pair beginning with Tripureśī, [the letters] Ādyā and the following. (171)
Having joined Śiva and Candra together, one should place Śiva on the third [finger];
this is the seat of the Tripurāśrīti-cakra, located in the region of the buttocks.

169–172 | Now, he describes the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) of the six seats with the words beginning "Then" (*atha tataḥ*). Among these, he first describes the ritual placement of the initial seat with the words "Tripureśī. Here, "Tripureśī" refers to the three seed-syllables (*bīja*) of Bālā. This was stated by the author of the *Tantrasāra*: "At the end of Bālā, [the mantra] 'Salutation to the one seated upon the ocean of nectar' (*amṛtārṇavāsanāya namaḥ*) is for the two feet. This ritual placement ends with the word "salutation" (*namaḥ*); it is the same everywhere.
From the [scriptural] vision: likewise, one should place [the mantra] "aiḥ klīṃ sauḥ, obeisance to the seat of nectar" (amṛtāsanāya namaḥ) on the two feet.
The great mantra for the seat, preceded by the word "ocean of nectar" (amṛtārṇava), should be placed on the two feet.

According to the statement of the *Yāmala*, however, the mantra results as exactly that which is adopted in the *Tantrasāra*: "ai klīṃ sauḥ, obeisance to the one seated upon the ocean of nectar" (*amṛtārṇavāsanāya namaḥ*). The author of the *Tantrasāra* has likewise written it in that very way.
He states the second [mantra]: "having uttered 'Kumārikā' (the Maiden), [then] 'Tripurasundarī' (the Beautiful One of the Three Cities)," and thereafter...

"Potāmbujāsana" means as follows: thus, one should perform the placement (*nyāsa*) on both knees with the mantra "aiḥ klīṃ sauḥ, obeisance to Tripurasundarī whose seat is the yellow lotus (*potāmbujāsana*). This is stated in that very same source:
"One should place 'obeisance' at the end of 'to her whose seat is the yellow lotus' upon the knee."

He states the third [mantra] with the words beginning "bālādi" and so forth. Having omitted the first of the three *bālā* seeds—namely, the seed "ai"—and having superimposed *māyā* (the seed *hrīṃ*) there, the meaning is that one should place the *māyā* seed in the position of the *vāgbhava* seed. Then [one says] "tripuravāsinī," then "ātmāsanāya," and then one should employ the word "namaḥ" as before. And thus:
The mantra-practitioner should cast the two seeds of Śiva and Candra into the two [seeds] of Bāla;
in the third, however, the seed of Śiva. Then follows Tripuramālinī, the seat for all mantras upon the liṅga, providing the splendor of the Goddess’s seat. (173)
Having abandoned the seed-syllable consisting of *vle*, one should write [the mantra] at the end of Tripura;
then, Siddheśvarī herself and the seat of the Siddhas for the object of attainment (*sādhya*) are at the anus.

The practical meaning is that one should perform the placement (*nyāsa*) on the two thighs with the mantra: *hrīṃ klīṃ sauḥ tripuravāsinyātmāsanāya namaḥ*. This is clearly stated in the *Yāmala* as cited in the *Tantrasāra*: "Having uttered *hrīṃ klīṃ sauḥ tripura*, one should then say the word *sundarī*."
At the end, one should place "ṅentaṃ devyāsanaṃ ca" and "namaḥ" upon the two thighs.
Thus [it is said]. Here, the specific [mantra] is: *namaḥ tripurasundarīdevyāsanāya*.

He states the fourth [seed-syllable] with the words beginning with "Śiva," and so forth. Having applied the letter *ha* (Śiva) to the first of the three Bālā seed-syllables previously mentioned—namely *aiṃ klīṃ sauḥ*—and the letter *ha* (Candra) to the second, one should "elevate" (utkṣipet) Śiva into the third; that is to say, one should extract it [there]. And thus: *aiṃ*...

By this [first rule], through its conjunction with the letter *ha*, *hai* is obtained; by the second [rule], through its conjunction with *killiṃ*, *haklīṃ* is obtained; and by the third [rule], through its conjunction with *sauri*, *hasauri* is obtained. Here, by the word "the moon" (*candram*), the seed-syllable of Śiva, which is signified by the term "Moon-crested One" (*candraśekhara*), is to be understood. This is clearly stated in the *Yāmala* as cited in the *Tantrasāra*:
One should place [the syllables] "haiṃ haklīṃ hasaurante tripuravāsinī" and "cakrāsanāya namaḥ" with this mantra upon the two buttocks.

Thus, the practice is as follows: *haiṃ haklīṃ hasauḥ tripurāśrīcakrāsanāya namaḥ*. However, according to the *Niruktayāmala*, the specific variation is "Tripuravāsinī. Regarding the phrase "in the region of the buttocks" (*sphic-deśake nitambe*), verses 173–174 state: he speaks of the fifth [seed-syllable] with the words beginning "Bālā," etc.; here too, among the previously mentioned *Bālā* seed-syllables, it is the first.
The meaning is that one should insert the *śivabīja*, the letter *ha*, and the *candrabīja*, the letter *sa*, into each of the two *bālā* seeds, namely *aiṃ* and *klīṃ*.

Thus, by joining *ha* and *sa* with *aiṃ*, one obtains *hasaiṃ*; and by joining them with *klīṃ*, one obtains *hasaklīṃ*. In the third seed, *klīṃ*, when joined with the *śivabīja* alone, it becomes simply *hasauṃ*. Then follows *tripuramālinī*, and after that—

"Obeisance to the seat of all mantras. Thus, the meaning is that one should perform the placement (*nyāsa*) on the *liṅga* with the mantra: *hasaiṃ hasaklīṃ hasauḥ tripuramālinī-sarvamantrāsanāya namaḥ*.
(This concludes the instruction for the six-limbed placement (*ṣaḍaṅganyāsa*) and the sequence for the placement of the eight goddesses beginning with Vaśinī.)
Having performed the six-limbed ritual as before, one should install the group of eight beginning with Vaśinī;
then, by means of the eight groups [of consonants] in their proper order, one should extract the seed-syllable consisting of the letter *va*.
One should place Vaśinī on the head, conjoined with Kalahrīṃ;
and in the skull, one should place the final letter of the dental class (ta), joined with the earth (la) and the wind (ya).
One should place Modinī, the deity of speech, between the eyebrows;
[one should place] Vāyu, joined with the nasal sound (nāda) and the bindu, from the left ear of the earth.
One should place Vimalā at the throat; the third letter of the *ca*-group, together with Kāla, Kṣmā, Anta, and the left eye, one should place Aruṇā at the heart. (178)

The sixth [mantra] is stated with the words "of the Goddess" (devyā) and so forth. Accordingly, from the sequence *hrīṃ klīṃ sauḥ*, one should omit *sauḥ*—the splendor of the seat—and instead inscribe *vlū~* there. Thus, the result is that one should install [the mantra] at the anus as follows: *hrīṃ klīṃ vlū~ tripurasundarīsādhyasiddhāsanāya namaḥ*. This is precisely what the authors of the *Tripurārcanarahasya* maintain.

175–178 | Regarding the phrase "the six-limbed" (*ṣaḍaṅga*): by the statement "having performed the six-limbed placement (*nyāsa*) as before," it should be understood that one performs the previously mentioned six-limbed placement according to the sequence to be described—either by repeating the root mantra twice with this [verse] beginning with "by this young girl" (*bālayā*), or by the [sequence] beginning with "the wise one" (*sudhīḥ*). However, the author of the *Tantrasāra* [states]:
Omniscience, eternal satisfaction, primordial awakening, sovereignty, unimpaired power, and infinity— these six, beginning with Śiva, are said by the Śivādyas to be the six limbs of Śiva and Śivā.
Having joined the name at the end of the seed-syllable (*bīja*), endowed with the [respective] *jāti* [mantric suffixes], the six-limbed (*ṣaḍaṅga*) rite is performed.

Thus, according to the authority of the *Navaratneśvara*, the six-limbed assignment (*ṣaḍaṅganyāsa*) is declared in this sequence: *aiḥ / Obeisance to the heart of Śrī Mahātripurasundarī, whose power is omniscience*. *klīḥ / Svāhā to the head of Śrī Mahātripurasundarī, whose power is eternal satisfaction*. In this manner, the six-limbed assignment is described.
However, because it says "having performed as before" (*pūrvavat kṛtvā*) here, it should be understood that this sequence is indeed different from that stated by Navaratneśvara.

Now, he describes the placement (*nyāsa*) of Vaśinī and the others with the words beginning "the group of eight starting with Vaśinī" (*vaśinyādyaṣṭakam*). One should place the group of eight starting with Vaśinī in sequence upon the eight locations beginning with the aperture of Brahmā (*brahmarandhra*) and ending with all the limbs, together with the eight groups of consonants.

The connection [is as follows]: the group of eight beginning with Vaśinī consists of those named Vaśinī, Kāmeśī, Modinī, Vimalā, Aruṇā, Jayinī, Sarveśī, and Kaulinī, which will be described later. Regarding that, he first states the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) with the verse beginning "consisting of *valū*" and ending with "on the head. By this [method], [the sequence] from *aṃ* up to *aḥ* [is established].

Then, one should place the group of vowels (*svaravarga*), followed by *balūṃ*, and then "Obeisance to Vaśinī Vāgdevatā" upon the crown at the aperture of Brahmā (*brahmarandhra*); this is the meaning. Regarding this, it is stated in the ninth chapter of the *Gandharvatantra*:
"Fire, Varuṇa, and Śakra, adorned with the sixth vowel."

"Endowed with the *nāda*, *bindu*, and *kalā*, followed by the word 'Vaśinī', and the Goddess of Speech (*Vāgdevatā*) in the dative case, one should install [the seed-syllables] with the vowels preceded by 'Namaḥ'.
Thus it is stated; and in the fourteenth chapter of the *Jñānārṇava*:
O beloved, O Goddess of virtuous vows, one should write the seed-syllable at the end of the vowels, followed by the letter *pha* with fire (*ra*) and earth (*la*),
adorned with the left ear (*u*), and marked with the bindu and nāda;
thus one should worship Vaśinī, the deity of speech.

Furthermore, from the observation of the sequence of nyāsa described above, it appears very clearly that after the pronunciation of the vowels beginning with *a* and ending with *visarga*, one should utter *rava-lūm* and then recite *vaśinīvāgdevatāyai namaḥ*. In the *Tantrasāra* as well, only *rava-lūm* is seen.
As for the reading *valūm-ātmakam* found in its source [the *Tantrāloka*], it is either a scribal error or perhaps accepted in other tantras.

May those who delight in the Tantras forgive us, for even though we were in doubt, we have, having no other recourse, performed the extraction of the mantra (*mantroddhāra*) strictly according to the root text.

He states the second [mantra] with the passage beginning with "Kāmeśīm" and ending with "kapāle tu. Thus, one should first place the *ka*-group along with its nasalization (*anusvāra*), then "kalahrīṃ," and then "kāmeśvarīvāgdevatāyai namaḥ" on the forehead. He explains this clearly:
In the ninth chapter of the Gandharva Tantra:
"Mādana is mounted upon Śakra; after that comes Mahāmāyā.
This is to be known as Kāmeśvarī, [represented] by the *ka*-group on the forehead. Thus it is said.

He states the third [seed-syllable] with the passage beginning with "the end of the *tavarga*" and ending with "one should install. Here too, one should take the *cavarga* together with the *anusvāra*, followed by the *tavarga* ending in *na*; that *na* is joined with the letter *va* (which ends the *tavarga*), with the earth (*bhū*) which is the letter *la*, with *māyā* which is the long *ī*, and by implication also with the *bindu*. By this, the syllable *navalī* is obtained. Then, [it is used] for Modinī Vāgdevatā.

The connection is that one should place the syllable *namaḥ* between the eyebrows. This is clearly stated in the fourteenth chapter of the Jñānārṇava: "At the end of the *ca*-group [the letter *ja*], followed by the letters *dha* and *la*, conjoined with the fourth vowel (*au*), one should worship Modinī, the deity of speech, immediately thereafter."
Also in the ninth chapter of the *Gandharva-tantra*: "The letter ending in 'dh', Varuṇa, and Indra, with the fourth vowel and the bindu—
this is indeed the goddess Modinī, [to be worshipped] between the eyebrows with the syllables ca, va, rva, and ka."

He states the fourth [mantra] with the passage beginning with "vāyum" and ending with "kaṇṭhe. Here, one should first place the ṭa-group (ṭa, ṭha, ḍa, ḍha, ṇa) together with the anusvāra; then the letter *ya* for "vāyu"; then the letter *la* for "bhūḥ" from the left ear; and the letter *ū* from the left ear—joined with those two and endowed with the *nāda* and *bindu*. Then, one should place [the mantra] at the throat with: "Oṃ Vimalāvāgdaivatāyai namaḥ. Thus it has been said:
In the ninth chapter of the *Gandharvatantra* (p. 478):
"Likewise, one should place [the syllable] consisting of Śiva, Soma, Earth, Water, Fire, and Earth at the navel; and the third letter of the *ca*-group for Jayinī."

One should place [the syllable] joined with *kāma* (K), *vahni* (R), *marut* (Y), the left ear (*vāmakarṇa*) (U), and the bindu (M) at the *mūlādhāra*. Then, one should place *sarveśī*, joined with *nṛsiṃha* (N), *kāla* (K), *vahni* (R), and the left eye (I), as *kaulinī* upon the ear. 180.

"O Goddess, [the syllable] Vāyu (Ya), Purandara (Ra), adorned with the sixth vowel (Ū), joined with Nāda, Bindu, and Kalā—this is declared to be Vimale; it should be placed in the region of the throat together with the Ṭa-group, O Pārvatī. Thus [it is said].

[The mantra] from "of the fifth [varga], the *ca*-group," etc., up to "one should place it in the heart. Here, first is the *ta*-group with the *anusvāra*; then the third letter of the *ca*-group, which is *ja*; then "the end of time and earth with the left eye": "time" (*kāla*) is the letter *ma*;
"that which has earth at its end" (*kṣmānta*) is the letter *ra*; and the "left eye" (*vāmanetra*) is the vowel *ī*. By this, *jamarī* is obtained.

Then, one should place [the seed-syllable] "Oṃ Aruṇāyai Vāgdevatāyai Namaḥ" in the heart. As for what is seen in the *Tantrasāra* following "Jamalī"—namely "Aruṇāyai" and so forth—that appears to be a mere error. In the ninth chapter of the *Gandharvatantra*:
"The letter 'Cha' (with bindu), the letter 'Bha' (with bindu), the fire (Ra), with the fourth vowel and the bindu."
The goddess of speech, the daughter of Aruṇa, resides in the heart with the *tavarga* consonants.
Because in this context, by the word "flame" (*jvalana*), the seed-syllable of fire, namely the letter *ra*, is clearly designated; and also in the fourteenth chapter of the *Jñānārṇava*:
"At the end of the *ta*-group, [the syllable] beginning with *ja* and the earth [letter], adorned with the left eye."
One should worship the goddess of speech, who is red in color and whose seed-syllable is marked with the *bindu* and *nāda*.

In this statement, by the phrase "beginning with earth" (*kṣmādyam*), there is an understanding of the letter *ra* itself, which belongs to the element of fire; however, it is in no way possible for the term "beginning with earth" (*kṣmādyam*) to denote the seed-syllable of earth (*pṛthvībīja*). As for the reading of the *Jñānārṇava* verse seen in modern printed editions of the *Tantrasāra*, namely "ending with earth after *ja*" (*jamakṣmāntam*), in that case, resorting to a *bahuvrīhi* compound is indeed correct.

179–180 | He states the sixth [mantra] with the words beginning with *śiva* and ending with *nābhau*. Here, first is the labial class (*pavarga*) together with its nasal (*anusvāra*), followed by *śiva* and so forth. *Śiva* is the letter *ha*; *Soma* is the letter *sa*; *Mahī* (Earth) is the letter *la*; *Toya* (Water) is the letter *va*;
*Vahni-bhūḥ* (Fire-born) is the letter *ya*, according to the Vedic revelation: "From space [came] air, from air fire," and so on. Then follows *ūṃ*. By this [is meant]: *ha sa la va yum*.
It is obtained. And then one should place [the mantra] "Obeisance to the victorious Goddess of Speech" at the navel. This is clearly stated in the ninth chapter of the Gandharva-tantra (p.
479): "And then, O Goddess, there is Jayinī, Nakulī, Soma, and Śakra."

"The seed-syllable of Vāyu, belonging to Varuṇa, adorned with the sixth vowel, is declared to be in the region of the navel along with the *pa*-group, O fair-faced one. Thus [it is said]. He states the seventh [seed-syllable] with the passage beginning with "of the *ca*-group" and ending with "the Mistress of All. Here, first is the *ya*-group, and then...
The third letter of the *ca*-group is the letter *ja*; *kāma* is the letter *ka*; *vahni* is the letter *ra*; and *marut* is the letter *ya*.

This [letter *ya*] is adorned with the left ear (*vāmakarṇa*), the bindu, the vowel *ū*, and the *anusvāra*. By this, it follows that after the *ya*-group comes *jara-yūm*. However, according to the *Gandharvajñānārṇava Tantra*, the usage *jhama-ra-yūm* is possible.

Furthermore, because the author of the *Śrīmat-tantrasāra* has stated exactly the same, we understand that the readings "the fourth of the *ca*-group" (*cavargasya caturthakam*) and "time" (*kāla*) have undergone a change of state into "the third" (*tṛtīyakam*) and "desire" (*kāma*) respectively due to the negligence of scribes. And so it is said in the ninth chapter of the *Gandharva-tantra*:

"Then [there is] the letter *ja*, followed by *bha*, then the letter *ra* conjoined with the seed-syllable of air (*ya*), joined with the sixth vowel (*ū*), and endowed with the *nāda*, *bindu*, and *kalā*;
[this is] Sarveśvarī with the *ya*-group, in the lotus called Svādhiṣṭhāna. Thus it is said.

And in the fourteenth chapter of the Jñānārṇava: "At the end of the *ya*-group [the letter *ra*], conjoined with the letter *ja*, the *kāla* (the letter *ha*), and the letter *repha* (the letter *ra*),
and enriched by *ūm*, one should worship the Goddess who is the Mistress of All Speech."

Thus it has been stated. And in this way, one should understand that according to the *Gandharvajñānārṇava*, [the mantra] culminates as follows: "yaṃ raṃ laṃ vaṃ jha ma ra yūṃ, salutation to the Goddess of Speech, Sarveśvarī.
He states the eighth [mantra] with the words beginning with "Nṛsiṃha" and ending with "one should place upon the ears"; "conjoined" (*saṃyuktam*) is an adverbial modifier of the action.
Alternatively, "sayuktām" may be the correct reading. Here, first the *śādivarga* (the group of letters from śa to kṣa), and then "nṛsiṃha" and so forth:

*nṛsiṃha* is the letter *kṣa*, *kāla* is the letter *ma*, and *vahni* is the letter *ra*, combined with the left eye, which is the fourth vowel (*ī*). By this, "kṣamarī" is obtained. Then, the meaning is that one should perform the placement (*nyāsa*) upon the ear with the mantra: "Obeisance to Kaulinīvāgdevatā. This is the placement.

"Root-support" (mūlādhāra) is the instruction given in the Gandharva Tantra. It is stated in that very work, in the ninth chapter: "O Maheśānī, [the syllable] Saṃvartaka is situated above the seed-syllable of Time (Ka);
then follows the seed-syllable of Fire (Ra), then Māyā (I), endowed with Nāda, Bindu, and Kalā."
In the mūlādhāra, Kaulinī is proclaimed to be associated with the śavarga.

Thus [it is said]. However, in the *Jñānārṇava*, this placement (*nyāsa*) is taught for all limbs. Accordingly, there, immediately after defining the nature of *nyāsa*, at the occasion of defining the locations, it says:
"In the regions of the head, forehead, between the eyebrows, throat, heart, and navel..."
"O Dear One, one should install the goddesses in sequence upon the support up to the *vyūhaka*. (p.
480) [This concludes] the instruction on the sixfold installation (*ṣoḍhānyāsa*).
Then, one should perform the sixfold installation by means of which one attains identification with That.
(Praise of the Sixfold Deposition):
By means of this, those beginning with Śiva and ending with Prajeśa become invincible. (181)
By him Rāma conquered Kārtavīryārjuna and others in battle twenty-one times; indeed, by him, the king of brahmins Durvāsas was subdued.
By him, whose speech was invincible and who wielded arrows, Rāma slew the night-stalkers who were arrogant due to their boons;
by him, Kṛṣṇa was indeed victorious in battle.
I declare this [mantra] to be equal to that, for it is the cause of invincibility;
by performing it, one attains the presence of the Greatly Powerful Lord of Tripura. || 184 ||
By the application of salutation, the practitioner can subdue poisons and the like, ward off all weapons and missiles, and even cause the death of enemies. 185.
One might cause trees, images, and mountains to split by means of a prostration;
yet none can endure that salutation except Viṣṇu and Śiva.
Seeing a practitioner performing the ritual placement (nyāsa) without Gaṇeśa, the Lord of the Lotus, and without Śrī Parameśvarī, the planetary spirits flee swiftly. || 187 ||
The mountains and other such things tremble, as do all other divine forms,
as well as spirits, ghosts, piśācas, and the like, along with dānavas, rākṣasas, and birds.
The Daityas, Gandharvas, and Siddhas flee, overcome by fear;
the Dākinīs and others, the great medicinal herbs, and the Mahoragas all flee away. (189)
The sun, the moon, and all others tremble, terrified by the bow;
diseases flee in haste, abandoning those who are ill. (190)
Even by the satisfaction of the touch of his hand, the most dreadful beings who have become pretas attain coolness merely from the touch of his body. (191)
Upon seeing him, all weapons, such as the Brahmāstra and others, become peaceful;
he attains freedom from old age and death, and the Goddess Lakṣmī never leaves his body.
Even the most terrible sins attain peace at that very moment;
having accomplished the sixfold deposition (ṣoḍhānyāsa), what is there in the three worlds that cannot be achieved? 193.
For by his mere contemplation, the powers of attraction, immobilization, and so forth, are accomplished;
therefore, I shall here proclaim the sixfold [practice], which is the most essential of the essential. (194)
(The Enumeration of the Sixfold Installations constituting the Ṣoḍhā-nyāsa):
The first installation is with the Gaṇeśas; the second is considered to be with the Planets;
the third should be with the Lunar Mansions; and the fourth with the Yoginīs.
The fifth placement is by means of the zodiac signs (rāśi), and the sixth is said to be by means of the sacred seats (pīṭha). || 195 ||
(The threefold nature of the sixfold [rite]:
That sixfold [rite] is said to be of three kinds: the small, the middling, and the superior.
The small is said to be fruitless, while the middling shall be fruitful. (196)

195. Having thus declared the praise of the sixfold deposition (*ṣoḍhānyāsa*) for the purpose of making it manifest to practitioners, he indicates the six types of depositions beginning with Gaṇeśa that constitute its components, starting with the words "by the Gaṇeśas," etc.
196–197. Next, according to the *Kuloḍḍīśamata*, he demonstrates the threefold nature of the sixfold deposition, starting with the word "sixfold," etc.

Regarding that, he states the nature of the Great Ṣoḍhā: "If *māyā* follows the seed-syllable *śrīmiti* [which is] *lakṣmīḥ*, it is the supreme Great Ṣoḍhā of Lakṣmī; if *kāma* follows *māyā*... (The authoritative status of this [text] is corroborated by the Tantras).
In the work titled Kuloḍḍīśa, however, such a method is recorded. || 197 ||
(Regarding the different ritual procedures for the application of the seed-syllable from the east:

One who is composed should place [the syllables] upon the body either with Vāk, Māyā, and Kamalā, or with their respective enclosures, or with the preceding [syllables] joined with Ramā and Māyā, or with Madana. 198.
(Meditation on the Gaṇeśas to be installed:
Resembling the young rising sun, with elephant faces and three eyes,
holding in their hands the noose, the goad, the boon-granting gesture, and the gesture of fearlessness, and accompanied by their Śaktis.
The wise practitioner should place these upon the body, just like the Mātṛkā-nyāsa. || 199 ||

The seed-syllables *hrīṃ* and *klīṃ*—the latter being the "seed of desire"—should be used. By this it is meant that here one should first utter *hrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ* and then perform the ritual deposition (*nyāsa*) with Vighneśvara and the others. This indeed is the doctrine of the Kuloḍḍīśa. This application of seed-syllables should be understood to apply to all six types of deposition, beginning with that of Gaṇeśa.

198. He states other sequences with the words beginning "vāk" (speech), etc. "Vāk" is the *vāgbhava* seed-syllable *aiṃ*; "māyā" is *hrīṃ*; "kamalā" is *śrīṃ*. Thus, having uttered *aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ*, one should perform the placement (*nyāsa*) according to the sequence to be described; this is another ritual procedure (*kalpa*).
This very one has been adopted by the authors of the *Tantrasāra*. Regarding the phrase "or with its enclosures": likewise, having uttered *aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ*, [one places] *aṃ*.

Having recited the syllables and deities to be deposited in the sequence beginning with "Salutation to Vighneśvara and Śrī," one should again utter "Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ"; this is another ritual procedure (*kalpa*). He states another ritual procedure: "With *ramā*. The connection is that one should deposit [the syllables] with the preceding ones joined together, namely with the *madanabījas* (kāmabījas) conjoined with *ramā* (Śrī) and *māyā* (Hrīṃ). Thus, in this ritual procedure, [the seed-syllables are] *Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Klīṃ*.

It has been stated that one should perform the placement (nyāsa) after first having applied [the mantras]. These varieties of the sequence for the conjunction of seed-syllables (bīja-yoga) are also to be adopted by practitioners in all six types of Gaṇeśa-nyāsa and the others.
Regarding the question of what forms the Gaṇeśas to be placed should have, he says: "taruṇa... (young). Here, [they are described as] "resembling the rising sun."

In the second chapter of the *Jñānārṇava*, and in the *Tripurārcanarahasya*, the reading "resembling the rising sun" (*taruṇādityasaṅkāśān*) is observed. Thus, the intended meaning is that one should meditate upon the Gaṇapatis as having such a form and then perform the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) according to the sequence to be described. For this very reason, after stating "resembling the rising sun" in the fourteenth chapter of the *Jñānārṇava*—
(The ritual placement of the seer and so forth for this [mantra]): Dakṣiṇāmūrti shall be the seer, and Gāyatrī is said to be the meter;
one should employ the deity Mahāgaṇapati in the form of Virāj. (200)
[The Nyāsa of Gaṇeśa (1)] Vighneśvara is joined with Śrī; likewise, Vighnarāja with Hrī;
Vināyaka with Tuṣṭi; and Śivottama is joined with Śānti. || 201 ||
"Having meditated, O Goddess, one should then perform the placement (nyāsa) in the manner of the Mātṛkā-nyāsa.

Thus it is said. By this, the statement in the root text—that "the wise [practitioner] should do so like the Mātṛkā-nyāsa"—is further confirmed. By the phrase "in the manner of the Mātṛkā-nyāsa," it is stated that the placement should be performed sequentially upon the parts of the body, such as the head, face, and so forth, as specified in the Mātṛkā-nyāsa.
200. Regarding that, he states the placement [of the mantra] upon the first seer and so forth, beginning with the words "The Seer" (ṛṣi). Accordingly, Dakṣiṇāmūrti says:
"It should be known that the Seer is [Gautama], the metre is Gāyatrī, the deity is Mahāgaṇapati, and its application (viniyoga) is in the form of Virāṭ.
However, in the eighth chapter of the Gandharva Tantra:

"Nārāyaṇa is declared its seer (ṛṣi), and Anuṣṭubh is cited as its meter (chandas)"—by such statements, a difference in sequence is observed in the definition of the seer and other elements. Furthermore, in the *Tantrasāra*, the seer and other elements are defined differently, stating "the Bṛhadāraṇyaka is the seer, Anuṣṭubh is the meter," and so forth. Thus, because such differences of opinion are seen here:
"One should adopt whichever one of these positions accords with the tradition of one's own guru; this is the general direction.

(201) Having thus demonstrated the application of the seed-syllables (*bījayoga*) and the ritual placement of the seers (*ṛṣinyāsa*) and so forth from the preceding section, he now describes the sequence of ritual placements (*nyāsaparipāṭī*) with the passage beginning "Vighneśvara" and ending with "the placement of Gaṇeśa has been indicated. Here, [the letters] beginning with the letter *a* and ending with the letter *kṣa*...

The meaning is as follows: because it will be stated later that "the wise one should place [them] together with the moon" (*sacandraiḥ*), and because it was previously mentioned that "the intelligent one [should do so] like the Mātṛkā-nyāsa," the wise practitioner should, according to the method of the Mātṛkā-nyāsa, utter each individual syllable beginning with *aṃ* and *āṃ* in the sequence starting from the head and mouth, and then place the deities to be described, such as Vighneśvara and the others. And thus:
(1) One sequence is in the form: *hrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ aṃ vighneśvara śrībhyāṃ namaḥ*, and so forth.
(2) The second is in the form: *aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ aḥ vighneśvara śrībhyāṃ namaḥ*, and so forth. (3) The third is in the form: *aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ aḥ vighneśvara śrībhyāṃ namaḥ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ*, and so forth.
(4) The fourth [form] is in the manner of: *śrī hrīṃ klīṃ vighneśvara śrībhyāṃ namaḥ*, and so forth; this is how it should be understood.
However, in the eighth chapter of the *Gandharva-tantra*, it says:
"O Goddess, [the mantra is] for Vighnarāja, and after that, *namaḥ* to Śrī."
To Vināyaka, for contentment and for peace, and to Śivottama.
Vighnakṛt is joined with Sṛṣṭi, and Vighnakartā is with Sarasvatī;
Vighnarāj is joined with Rati, and Gaṇanāyaka is with Medhā. || 202 ||
Ekadanta and Śānti; Dvidanta accompanied by Kāminī; Gajavaktra and Mohinī; Nirañjana endowed with matted locks. || 203 ||
Kapardin and likewise Dīrghavaktra, Mālinī;
Saṅkarṣaṇa and likewise Nandā, Surasā and Vṛṣadhvaja. (204)
Gaṇanātha, Kāmarūpa, and Gajendra were joined by Subhrū. || 205 ||
Śūrpakarṇa with Jayinī, Trilocana with Satyā, Lambodara with Vighneśī, and Mahānāda with Svarūpiṇī. || 206 ||
Caturmūrti, who grants desires, is united with Sadāśiva;
and she named Madavihvalā is joined with Āmoda and Vikaṭā. || 207 ||
Durmukha joined with Ghūrṇā, Sumukha joined with Bhūti, and likewise Pramoda; these, together with Bhūmi and Eka accompanied by Pāda, constitute the group. (208)
Dvijihva is joined with Ramā; Mānuṣī is joined with Surayukta;
and she who is named Makaradhvajā is joined with Vīreśvara. || 209 ||

Because of such separate indications in the dative case (*caturthyanta*) here and there—such as "to Vighnarāja, obeisance to Śrī" and "to Vināyaka, obeisance to Tuṣṭi"—it appears that, according to that system, the sequence of ritual application (*prayogakrama*) takes the form of these specific formulas. However, in this citation from the *Gandharvatantra*, the names of Vighneśvara and Śrī, who are to be first installed, are not seen; the same is the case in the *Tripurārcanarahasya*. [In the] *Jñānārṇava*...
However, in the fourteenth chapter,

the placement (*nyāsa*) of Vighneśvara and Śrī is first mentioned by means of the passage beginning with "Vighneśvara as well as Śrī, and likewise Vighnarāja with Hrī. Therefore, according to that very system, [the procedure] is applied here.
First, there is the mention of Vighneśvara and Śrī; it is exactly the same in the *Tantrasāra*. The rest is clear. (p.
485) Manmatha is joined with Piṅgalā, is boon-granting, and is endowed with a frown;
likewise Vāmadeva with Lajjā, and between them is Raktatuṇḍa.
Afterwards, [there is] Dīrghaghoṇānvita, Dviraṇḍaka, and Dhanurdhara; Senānī joined with Yāminī, and Grāmaṇī joined with Rātri. || 211 ||
Darkness joined with moonlight, the stainless radiance of the moon,
the swaying of a rider on an intoxicated mount, and the flickering glance of one with matted hair.
One with a shaven head is endowed with supernatural powers (ṛddhi); one with a sword is joined with misfortune;
one who is excellent is joined with good fortune; and one with the shoulders of a bull is joined with auspiciousness (śivā).
Durgā is accompanied by Bhakṣyapriyā, Gaṇa by Gṛhakāntā,
Meghanāda by Kālikā, and Gaṇeśa by Analajihvā.
The wise one should perform the placement [of letters] starting from 'a' and ending with 'kṣa', accompanied by the moon;
this is declared as the Gaṇeśa-nyāsa. (The promise regarding Graha-nyāsa) (2)
And the placement of the planets (grahanyāsa) is now described. || 215 ||
(Therein is the description of the colors of the planets: The Sun is red, the Moon is white, and Mars is red in color;
Mercury is dark, Jupiter is yellow, and the son of Bhṛgu (Venus) is pale-white.
One should meditate upon Saturn as black, dark, and smoky, preceded by the Sun.

215. Having thus taught the first of the six nyāsas that constitute the limbs of the *ṣoḍhā-nyāsa*, namely the *gaṇeśanyāsa*, he now describes the second, the *grahanyāsa*, with the words beginning "graha" and so forth.
216. Regarding the word "tamaḥ": *tamaḥ* refers to Rāhu; as Amarasimha states, "tamastu rāhuḥ. [The word] "kṛṣṇam" [is to be understood] with reference to both Śani and Tamas (Rāhu).
The connection [is as follows]: the dark color of Saturn—[his] form is:
"The son of the Sun (Sauri), four-armed, dark-complexioned, clad in black garments, and mounted upon a vulture. (p.
486) (His Form)
These [deities] assume forms at will, adorned with divine garments;
they rest their hands upon their beautiful left thighs and grant fearlessness with their right hands. (217)
(The Sequence of Nyāsa):
One should place the Sun (arka) with the vowels beyond the heart, then the Moon (vidhu) in the middle of the bow;
then one should place Mars (kuja) with the four letters beginning with 'ya' in the two lotus-eyes.

One should place the wise one (Buddha) with the letter *ka* and so forth in one's own heart; the preceptor of the gods (Bṛhaspati) with the first group of letters (*ca* and so forth), and [the others] with the five letters beginning with *ṭa*, in the regions starting from the heart in due order.
By this [verse], the black color of Rāhu is indicated: "Having meditated upon Rāhu as a Śūdra, born of Malaya, twelve finger-breadths in height,
black in complexion and clad in black garments, seated upon a lion-throne, one should likewise invoke him."
By this [verse], the smoke-colored nature of Ketu is also indicated: "The group of Ketus belonging to Kauśadvīpa, following the Jaiminīya school, measuring six finger-breadths,
smoke-colored, seated upon a vulture, having a distorted face— one should summon the Śūdra."

By this, the reality of the planetary sacrifice (*grahayāga*) has been established. Regarding the phrase "preceded by Ravi" (*ravipūrvakam*): since *ravi* is the letter *ka*, and by the force of the meaning "that which has *ravi* as its predecessor," the planet Ketu is understood by the term *ravipūrvaka*, because the letter *ka* is the first constituent part of his name. However, in the fourteenth chapter of the *Jñānārṇava*, a distinction is observed in the description of the letters of the planets:

One should contemplate [the gems] as ruby, white, red, dark, yellow, and pale; smoky-black, black-smoky, and smoke-gray; as well as those headed by the Sun, who can assume any form at will and are adorned with all ornaments. And so forth.

218. Now he teaches the sequence for the placement (*nyāsa*) of the planets, beginning with the words "the sun" (*arkam*). The connection is that one should place the sun (*arka*) by means of the vowels in the region below the heart (*hṛdaya*). Here too, as before, there is the conjunction with the seed-syllables of Māyā and the others; then follow the vowels from *a* to *visarga* accompanied by the *anusvāra*, and finally "salutation to Sūrya" (*sūryāya namaḥ*). Thus, [the mantra is]: *hrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ aṃ āṃ iṃ*.
The mantra concludes as follows: *īṃ uṃ ūṃ ṛṃ ṝṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ eṃ aiṃ oṃ auṃ aṃ aḥ sūryāya namaḥ*. This is stated in the ninth chapter of the *Gandharvatantra* (p. 487):
"Then, in the throat, [the syllables] beginning with *śu* and ending with *kha*, along with the group of letters beginning with *pa*..."
Then the Lord of Heroes (Vīrendra) should sequentially place Rāhu with the group of consonants (Śavarga) in the Maṇipūraka and the mouth,
and the ninth [planet], Ketu, with two hundred thousand [repetitions] in the region of the feet;
[this is the promise regarding the instruction for the Tārā-nyāsa].
Now the Tārā-nyāsa is described, which brings about auspiciousness and bestows the accomplishment of all aims. (219)
(Therein is the meditation on the Tārās:
Resembling the blazing fire of cosmic destruction, with hands granting boons and fearlessness, their hands joined in salutation, headed by Aśvinī, they are adorned with all ornaments. || 220 ||
Having first extracted the vowels, endowed with the moon and the bindu,
and having uttered "Sūryāya namaḥ," one should install them in the heart.

And so forth. This should be understood to apply to the [mantras] that are about to be mentioned as well. As for the sequence of ritual application seen in the *Tantrasāra* in the form "Obeisance to Āditya and Ruci," and so on—that was intended by its proponents [to mean]:
"One should place the Sun in the heart with the vowels, and the Moon together with the *ya*-group."
Because this [practice] is not found even in such statements as those in the fourteenth chapter of the *Jñānārṇava*, we have not included it here.
We understand, however, that the author of the *Tantrasāra* has devised this application by resorting to a different system.
Now, "in the middle of the bow" means in the middle of the eyebrows. "By the four letters beginning with *ya*" refers to these: *yaṃ*, *raṃ*, *laṃ*, and *vaṃ*.

The connection is that one should place the Moon (vidhu). Here too, the sequence takes the form: *hrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ yaṃ raṃ laṃ vaṃ somāya namaḥ*, and so forth; this should be inferred for the [deities] to be mentioned hereafter as well. Now, regarding "with the five letters beginning with *ka*": the connection is that one should place the Moon in the two lotus-eyes using the five letters beginning with *ka*. Regarding "with the [letters] beginning with *ca*": using the *ca*-group (*cavarga*), as before, one should [place it] in one's own heart.

One should place Budha with the *ṭa*-group in the region of the heart—that is, above the heart; this means one should install Suraguru (Bṛhaspati). [Verse 219] Regarding "Śukram": one should place Śukra with the letters beginning with *ta* in the throat region; likewise, with the *pa*-group (*pavarga*), one places Śanaiścara in the Maṇipūraka, which is the navel lotus—this is the remainder of the sense. Likewise, one should place Rāhu with the *śa*-group in the mouth; and likewise, *la-*...
The connection is that the Lord of Heroes (*vīrendra*) should place the ninth [deity], Ketu, at the location of the feet with the two syllables *kṣā* and *laṃ kṣam*.

Although Saturn is not explicitly mentioned here, it should be understood that the placement of Śanaiścara occurs in the Maṇipūraka. This is clearly stated in the fourteenth chapter of the Jñānārṇava:
"Saturn is with the *pa*-group at the navel; Rāhu is in the mouth, along with the *śa*-group.
Thus [it is said]. Now, he promises to describe the placement (*nyāsa*) of the stars with the fourth quarter-verse beginning with "The star," etc.
(220). Therein, first, he describes the visualization (*dhyāna*) of Aśvinī and the others with a single verse beginning with "Blazing," etc., ending with "with hands in salutation."
Those by whom the hands have been employed for the sake of dance.
(The sequence of nyāsa: A-Ā would be Aśvinī first; likewise, the pair [I-Ī] is Bharaṇī.
U and ū belong to Kṛttikā, while ṛ, ṝ, ḷ, and ḹ belong to Rohiṇī. || 221 ||
And there may be Mṛgaśirā with *e*, Pūrvaphalgunī with *ai* and *ār*, Ārdrā with *o* and *au*, Punarvasu with *aṃ* and *aḥ*, and Puṣya with *kaṃ*, *kha*, and *ga*. || 222 ||
Aśleṣā is represented by *gha* and *ṅa*; Maghā by *cha* and *ja*; Uttarā [Phalgunī] by *jha*; Hastā by *ña*; Citrā is proclaimed by *ṭa* and *ṭha*; and Svātī is likewise declared. || 223 ||
Ḍa represents Viśākhā; ḍha and ṇa represent Anurādhā; furthermore, ta, tha, and da represent Jyeṣṭhā; dha and na represent Mūlā; and pa and pha represent Pūrvāṣāḍhā. || 224 ||
Ba and uttarā would be bha and mau; abhijit and śravaṇā would be ya and rau; la would be dhaniṣṭhā, and va and śau would likewise be śatabhiṣā. || 225 ||
The syllable *ṣa* corresponds to Pūrvabhādrapadā, and likewise *u* to Uttarā;
*la*, *kṣau*, and *revatāvarṇau* are the letters in sequence, or these are the letters [of the asterisms]. (226)

221–226 | Now, he demonstrates the sequence for the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) of the lunar mansions (*nakṣatra*), beginning with "a-ā syāt" and ending with "ime. Here too, as before, the seed-syllables previously mentioned—either by the rule "if Lakṣmī, Māyā, and Kāma are at the front" or by "with Vāk, Māyā, and Kamalā"—must be joined at the beginning [of the mantras], because they have been stated in a general sense; thus, according to the *Tantrasāra*—

This is because it is seen thus in the *Tripurārcanarahasya* and other texts. As for the locations of the ritual placement (*nyāsa*), he will describe them with the words: "On the forehead, the two eyes, the pair of ears, the two nostrils," and so forth. Accordingly, having first uttered either *hrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ*, or *aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ*, or any one of the others, one should then utter the vowels and consonants in the sequence beginning with *aṃ āṃ*, and so on.

Having pronounced [the seed-syllables] preceded by *prāptam* and ending with *namaḥ*, one should assign the lunar mansions beginning with Aśvinī. For the easy understanding of practitioners, a mere indication is shown as follows:
(1) *hrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ aṃ āṃ aśvinyai namaḥ* (on the forehead); this is the first sequence.
(2) *Ai Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Aṃ Āṃ* [Salutation to Aśvinī] on the forehead; such is the second form. (p.
489) [In that regard, there is another sequence: "The first pair, then one, then three, and then four."
In this manner, one by one and then two by two, [the vowels] proceed in sequence up to the fourteenth vowel.
The supreme practitioner should arrange one consonant, two, and a pair;
one, a pair, two, a couple, one, a couple, and a triad. (228)
One, then a triad, likewise one, one, one, then two;
again one, two, Rāma, Lakṣa, and the fourfold Aṃ. || 229 ||
Having offered [the oblation] in front of Aśvinī and the others, one should place them in sequence:
(the locations suitable for placement are) on the forehead, the two eyes, the pair of ears, and the two nostrils. || 230 ||
On the throat, on both shoulders, likewise on both elbows, on the pair of wrists, on both hands, on the navel, and on both hips. (231)
(3) *Ai Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Aṃ Āṃ Aśvinyai Namaḥ Ai Hrīṃ Śrīṃ* [on the forehead]—this is the third form.
(4) *Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Klīṃ Aṃ Āṃ Aśvinyai Namaḥ* [on the forehead]—this is the fourth form.
Having thus adopted one of these sequences according to the tradition of one's own guru, one should likewise perform the placement (*nyāsa*) for Bharaṇī and the other constellations.

The specific details for each instance will be stated by the author himself in the passage beginning with "the pair of *i*s," etc. The rest is clear. Now, he demonstrates a different sequence for the placement (*nyāsa*) of the stars (*tārā*), beginning with "Alternatively" (*athavā*).
Verses 227–229: In this placement of the stars, everything is exactly as before, except that at the beginning of the names of the lunar mansions (*nakṣatra*), [the seed-syllables are added].

He states the specific detail regarding the combination of those respective vowels and consonants with the words "the first pair," and so forth. Thus, before Aśvinī there are two: *aṃ* and *āṃ*; before Bharaṇī there is one: *iṃ*; before Kṛttikā there are three: *īṃ*, *uṃ*, and *ūṃ*;
before Rohiṇī there is a quartet: *ṛṃ*, *ṝṃ*, *ḷ*, and *ḹṃ*; and before Mṛgaśiras there is one: *eṃ*. In this manner, according to the sequence—

One should join the fourteen vowels ending in *au* to the preceding [consonants]; however, the application of *aṃ* and *aḥ* at the end of the consonants will be explained by himself in the section on Revatī. Thus, the sequence of practice takes such forms as *hrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ aṃ āṃ aśvinyai namaḥ*, and so forth. This should be understood to apply to the consonants as well; the meaning is that there are three syllables, namely *rāṃ maṃ haṃ*.
The rest is clear. He concludes the second alternative with the words "of Aśvinī and so forth. This is clear.
(230–231) Now he describes the locations for both types of nakṣatra-arrangements mentioned previously:
On the two thighs, on the pair of knees, on the pair of shanks, and on the pair of feet.
But in the case of twenty-eight [teeth], there should be two swellings on the neck. || 232 ||
(Conclusion of the Tārānyāsa; Instruction on the Yoginīnyāsa) (4) Having performed the Ṛkṣanyāsa, one should perform the Yoginīnyāsa. || 233 ||

(Therein is the meditation on the Ḍākinī: She has red eyes and a red complexion; she causes fear to common folk and holds a trident and a *khaṭvāṅga* in her hands, while holding a sword in her left hand and also a chalice filled with nectar; she has a single face.

One should meditate upon that Ḍākinī, who is exceedingly fierce with terrible fangs, the crusher of the host of enemies, who is intent on milk-rice offerings, and whose body is enveloped at the throat by nectar and clarified butter.
(The Nyāsa of the Ḍākinīs):
First, with the vowels, the pair ending in *ṭha* is conjoined with the fourth vowel [ū]; joined with *nāda*, *bindu*, and *kalā*, this is declared to be the pair of seed-syllables (*bīja*). (235)

By the words "on the forehead" and so forth, the meaning is as follows: one should assign the twenty-seven lunar mansions (*nakṣatras*) in this sequence: Aśvinī on the forehead; Bharaṇī and Kṛttikā on the right and left eyes; Rohiṇī and Mṛgaśiras on the right and left ears; Ārdrā and Punarvasu on the right and left nostrils. Regarding the word "eight": in this system, because Abhijit is counted twice, there are eight [mansions] here.

It should be understood that there are twenty-eight constellations (*nakṣatra*). The rest is clear. Having thus described the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) of the constellations, he teaches the necessity of performing the ritual placement of the *yoginīs* with the words beginning "yoginī" (verse 235).
Having thus described the visualization of Ḍākinī at the throat, he explains her ritual placement in that very same location:

By the words "with vowels" (*svaraiḥ*) and so forth: previously, the pair ending in *ṭha*—meaning the two *ḍa*s, since *ḍa* is the letter at the end of the *ṭha*-group—is characterized by the fourteen vowels beginning with *a*. Furthermore, that [pair] is "pierced by *pāśa* and the fourth," meaning it has attained a modified form through being pierced by *pāśa*, which is the vowel *ā*, and the "fourth," which is the fourth vowel *ī*. Thus...

"Endowed with the digits of *nāda* and *bindu*" refers to the pair of seed-syllables *ḍāṃ* and *ḍīṃ*; that is to say, the two seed-syllables *ḍāṃ* and *ḍīṃ*. Here too, as before, one should remember the application of the seed-syllables (*bījayoga*). By this, it follows that first come *hrīṃ*, *klīṃ*, and *śrīṃ*, then the vowels from *aṃ* up to *oṃ*, and finally *ḍāṃ* and *ḍīṃ*.

Then, [the syllables] beginning with *ḍa* and ending with *la*, adorned by the left ear, joined with the *nāda*, *bindu*, and *kalā*, are likewise followed by "Homage to Ḍākinī" (*ḍākinyai namaḥ*). (236)
Having uttered "Dākinī," she then departed from the skin-element;
she is the mistress of sixty-four million lakhs of yoginīs. (237)
One should say: "O you who bring all beings under your control, grant me your command!
Then, one should place the two protective *ḍākinīs* upon the sandals at the neck. (238)

236. Now, he states the remainder with the words beginning with "tataḥ" (then). Being adorned by the left ear and being joined with *nāda*, *bindu*, and *kalā* constitutes the final delimitation; by this, *ḍa ma la va ra yūṃ* is obtained. Then follows: *ḍākinyai namaḥ*.

And thus, one of the previously mentioned syllables such as *hrīṃ*, *klīṃ*, or *śrīṃ* follows, and thereafter it concludes with: *aṃ āṃ iṃ īṃ uṃ ūṃ ṛṃ ṝṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ eṃ aiṃ oṃ auṃ aṃ aḥ ḍāṃ ḍīṃ ḍa ma la va ra yūṃ ḍākinyai namaḥ*.

237–238 | Now he states the placement (*nyāsa*) of the *ḍākinī* sandals, beginning with the word "Ḍākinī. Thus, it concludes as follows: "O Ḍākinī, you who reside in the element of the skin, sovereign of sixty-four million *yoginīs*, subduer of all sentient beings, grant your command! Protect me, protect me! Salutation to the sandals of the Ḍākinī. The term "kaṭhata" means "the throat. One should place [the mantra] upon the Ḍākinī.
The meaning is that both of these, including her sandals, [are to be worshipped]. However, in the ninth chapter of the Gandharva Tantra, it says:
"First, having extracted the vowels provided with the moon-bindu (anusvāra), then follow the two final letters of the *ṭha*-group, subsequently pierced by the fourth [letter] of the *pāśa*."
The two seed-syllables (bījas) are said to be joined with Nāda, Bindu, and Kalā.
[These are] the final letter of the Ṭa-group (ṭha), the final letter of the Bha-group (bha), the seed-syllable of the Earth (la), the Water-element (va), Fire (ra), and Wind (ya).
Then, O Goddess, there is the left ear (śa), conjoined with Nāda, Bindu, and Kalā.
Having addressed the Ḍākinī at the end with "Obeisance to the Ḍākinī" (ḍākinyai namaḥ),
and then having uttered [the mantra] beginning with "Dugdhātugata," followed by the sixty-four words,
and finally "Yoginīsvāminī" at the end of the hundred-thousand-crore words.
One should utter "sarvasattvavaśam," followed by the word "kari. Then, one should say, "Give me your command," and after that, the two words "mama vikri" (or "mama rakṣa").
In such cases, the sequence is generally seen to be the same; however, in this instance, one should place the *pādukā* upon the throat explicitly.
(The Assignment of the Deities of the Ḍākinī Retinue): Amṛtākarṣiṇī, Indrāṇī, Īśānī, and Ūrdhvakeśinī;
Ṛddhidā, Ṛṣikā, and likewise Ḷkā and Lṛkaikapādikā.
Then follows the one named Aiśvaryadātmikā, and after that, Oṃkāriṇī.

The practitioner of mantra, having visualized her as being like a ḍākinī, should arrange [the syllables] all around—consisting of medicinal herbs, of the nature of equanimity, endowed with the vowels, and endowed with the consonants. (240)
(The meditation on Rākiṇī:

One should meditate upon the goddess who is dark-complexioned, holding a trident and a lotus in her hands, and possessing a hand with a *ḍamaru* drum; she carries a sharp vajra, has three red eyes, and is radiant with the luster of her bared fangs and teeth set within a frown of knitted brows.

One should meditate upon that radiant Rākiṇī, the goddess of gods, who resides in the heart-lotus, who is the sole mistress of the blood-element, whose mind is attached to white food, and who bestows desired fruits. || 241 ||
(The Nyāsa of Rākiṇī):

Then, with the consonants *ka* and *ṭha*, one should utter the letter *ra* as before according to the distinction of vowels; one should then recite *ra-ma-la-va-ra-yā*, adorned by the left ear [the letter *u*] and the moon [the letter *i*]. (242)

Since it was previously stated, "Obeisance to Ḍākinī from the sight [of her]," it appears that the authors of the treatises intended the installation of the Ḍākinī’s sandals (ḍākinīpādukānyāsa) immediately after the installation of Ḍākinī herself. However, it should be understood that the sequence for the installation of Ḍākinī as described in the *Tantrasāra*— which follows the *Jñānārṇava*— is distinct from this one.
239–240 | Next, he teaches the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) of the yoginīs who form her retinue, beginning with the words "Amṛta" and so forth.
Since it will be stated here that they are "conjoined with vowels," one should first join each of the sixteen vowels, beginning with *a*, to the sixteen petals of the lotus called Viśuddha.
With the intention that one should place each of the [substances] beginning with *amṛta* on each individual petal, it is said, "one should arrange them all around" (verses 242–244).
Having described the visualization (*dhyāna*) of Rākiṇī with the words beginning "śyāmām" (verse 245), he states the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) with the words beginning "ka-ṭha-varṇaiḥ.
By "the letters *ka* and *ṭha*" is meant the letters starting from *ka* and ending with *ṭha*. And thus, following any one of the [seed-syllables] such as *hrīṃ*, *klīṃ*, or *śrīṃ*:
Having uttered "Kaṃ Rākiṇī" joined with the suffix -ṅe, and then the heart-mantra thereafter;
[this is for] Rākiṇī, who resides in the blood constituent, for thirty-two lakṣas and koṭis [of recitations]. || 243 ||
Having addressed her as "Yoginī-Svāminī," the subduer of all beings, one should then say: "Grant me your command, and protect me with the pair [of deities] and Rākiṇī. (244)
(The ritual placement of the deities of Rākiṇī’s retinue:
Thereafter, one should place [the letters] surrounding the Anāhata [cakra] with the consonants from *ka* to *ṭha*:
Kālarātri, Khātitā, Gāyatrī, and then Ghaṇṭikā. (245)
One should likewise install Ṅā, Vṛścikā, Cāmuṇḍā, Chāyā, Jayā, Jhaṅkāriṇī, Jñānā, and Ṭaṅkahastā. (246)
Having meditated on these [goddesses] and Ṭhaṅkārī in sequence, and the Hero as before,
the practitioner of mantra should then meditate on the goddess Lākinī in the twelve-spoked [cakra].

*Khaṃ gaṃ ghaṃ ṅaṃ caṃ chaṃ jaṃ jhaṃ ñaṃ ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ rāṃ rīṃ ra ma la va ra yūṃ rākiṇyai namaḥ*. After that, one should perform the placement (*nyāsa*) with: *Rākiṇyasṛgdhātugate dvātriṃśallakṣakoṭiyoginīsvāmini sarvasattvavaśaṅkari ājñāṃ dehi māṃ rakṣa rakṣa rākiṇīpādukāyai namaḥ*.

The result [of this] is as follows: although only the name "Rākiṇī" is mentioned here, the employment of the term *pādukā* (sandals/supernatural sandals) is to be understood according to the sequence previously stated (vv. 245–247). Now, he describes the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) of the deities who form Rākiṇī’s retinue, beginning with the words "in the Anāhata," etc. The phrase "one should place in the Anāhata" is also connected with what precedes it. "In the Anāhata" refers to the twelve-petaled heart-lotus. Regarding the syllables "ka-ṭha": [they are to be applied] according to the sequence previously mentioned.

Having placed Rākiṇī upon the pericarp of the lotus, the meaning is that one should place the twelve deities beginning with Kālarātri upon the twelve petals surrounding it; that is to say, by means of the twelve syllables beginning with *ka* and ending with *ṭha*, joined as previously described.
Thus: *kaṃ kālarātryai namaḥ*, *khaṃ khātitāyai namaḥ*, *gaṃ gāyatryai namaḥ*, *ghaṃ*...
One should know that the nyāsa is to be performed in the sequence beginning with "Ghaṇṭikāyai namaḥ" and "Ṅaṃ Vṛścikāyai namaḥ," ending with "Ṭhāṃ Kāryai.

As for the question of where, he says: "on the twelve-spoked [wheel]," which means on the Anāhata [cakra]. Next, he indicates the meditation on Lākinī with the passage ending in "one should meditate upon the goddess Lākinī."
(The Meditation on Lākinī:

One should meditate upon the black goddess, who has three faces, is graced with three eyes, possesses fangs, and has a fierce form; she holds a vajra, a spear, and a fine staff in her right hands, while her left hands display the gestures of fearlessness and granting boons.

Having meditated upon her situated in the lotus at the navel, shining with ten petals and a pericarp, the lord of practitioners should contemplate that Lākinī, who resides in flesh and whose heart is eager for rice cooked in molasses. || 248 ||
(The Nyāsa of Lākinī):
Then [the letters] from *ḍa* to *pha*, followed by *lāṃ līṃ la ma la va ra yāṃ*, joined with the left ear (*vāmakarṇa*), and also [the mantra] "Salutation to Lākinī" (*lākinyai namaḥ*). 249.
Then, when the practitioner recites "Lākinī," she resides in the flesh-element;
as before, there are sixteen lakṣas and ten million koṭis [of repetitions] in the Maṇipūraka.
(The Deposition of the Deities in the Retinue of Lākinī and the Instruction on the Meditation on Kākinī:
Ḍākinī, Ḍhaṅkārī, Ṇākinī, Tapasvinī, Thānavī, Dakṣiṇā, Dhātrī, Nādā, and likewise Pārvatī. (251)
Having meditated upon these [deities] ending with Phaṭkāriṇī in their proper sequence, one should install them with a concentrated mind;
then, conjoined with the letters from Ḍa to Pha, one should meditate upon Kākinī.
248. "Vajra" means that she holds a vajra and a śakti in her right and left hands respectively—this is the connection.

By the qualifying phrase "shining on the pericarp of the ten-petaled [lotus]," it is indicated that Lākinī is to be meditated upon within the pericarp of the *maṇipūra* lotus. "Gauḍī" means one whose mind is longing for the consumption of food mixed with molasses (*guḍa*).
249–250 | "Beginning with *ḍādi* and ending with *phānta*" and so forth. And likewise, as before, having uttered any one [of the seed-syllables] such as *hrīṃ* or *śrīṃ*, [one recites]:

*ḍaṃ ḍhaṃ ṇaṃ taṃ thaṃ daṃ dhaṃ naṃ paṃ phaṃ lāṃ līṃ la ma la va ra yūṃ lākinyai namaḥ*. Then, [one addresses] Lākinī, who resides in the flesh-element (*māṃsa-dhātu*) and is the mistress of sixteen hundred thousand million yoginīs.

"O subduer of all beings, grant your command; protect me, protect me! Homage to the sandals of Lākinī. Thus it follows that one should perform the placement (*nyāsa*) in the *maṇipūra*. (251–252) Now, he describes the placement of the ten members of Lākinī’s retinue upon the ten petals of the *maṇipūra*:
(The Meditation on Kākinī):
In the lotus called Svādhiṣṭhāna, which has six petals, one should visualize Kākinī, who resides within the fat;
she is yellow in color, holds a noose, a trident, a hand-drum, and the gesture of fearlessness.

One should meditate upon that Yoginī Kākinī, whose mind is attached to curd-rice, who is saluted by the best of gods, whose heart is intoxicated, and whose body is encircled by six petals beginning with *ba* and ending with *la*. || 253 ||

(The Kākinī-nyāsa: Then, from *ba* to *la*, as well as *kāṃ*, *kīṃ*, and *kamalavarayūm*; at the end, [recite] "obeisance to Kākinī" (*kākinyai namaḥ*), which is then placed upon the fat constituent (*medas*). 254.
One should install the eight hundred thousand yoginīs in the *svādhiṣṭhāna* [cakra];
having extracted the remainder as before, [this is] the installation of the deities of Kākinī’s retinue.
But [they are] with the vowels ending in 'ba' and 'la' in sequence. || 255 ||
Vajriṇī, Bhadrakālī, Mahāmāyā, Yaśasvinī, Rāmā, and Lambodarī—these one should install like the Kākinīs. (256)
Regarding the passage beginning with "Ḍākinī" and so forth: the meaning is that one should perform the placement (nyāsa) of Ḍākinī and the others, conjoined with the consonants from *ḍa* to *pha*.
Thus, the sequence of practical application results in forms such as: *ḍaṃ ḍākinyai namaḥ*, *ḍhaṃ ḍhaṅkāryai namaḥ*, *ṇaṃ ṇākinyai namaḥ*, and so on.

254–256 | Having thus described the meditation (*dhyāna*) on Kākinī, he states the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) with the words beginning "from *ba* to *la*" (*bādilāntam*), and so forth. Accordingly, after any one of the [seed-syllables] such as *hrīṃ*, *klīṃ*, or *śrīṃ*, [one recites]: *baṃ bhaṃ maṃ yaṃ raṃ laṃ kāṃ kīṃ ka ma la va ra yūṃ kākinyai namaḥ*. Then, [one places it] upon Kākinī, the mistress of the eight hundred thousand yoginīs residing in the marrow-element (*medodhātu*).

"O you who bring all beings under your control, grant me your command; protect me, protect me! Homage to the sandals of Kākinī. Thus one should place [the mantra] at the *svādhiṣṭhāna*. Now, he describes the placement of the deities of her retinue, beginning with "with the letters from *ba* to *la*," etc. And thus: *baṃ*...

The Goddess, whose nature is light, beautiful with three eyes and five radiant faces, holding in her hands a bow, an arrow, a noose, a goad, a book, and the gesture of knowledge;
she who crushes all fettered beings, residing within the bone, seated upon the lotus at the *mūlādhāra*.
One should meditate upon that Ḍākinī, who is full of affection for milk-rice and delighted by the intoxication of honey. || 257 ||
(The Deposition of the Śākinīs) Having meditated thus, the knower of mantras should extract the syllable of the first letter of the alphabet;
he should utter "SĀM SĪM SA MA LA VA RA YŪM," followed by the word "Śākinīm" joined with the dative suffix -ṄE. (258)
Then, having recited the heart-mantra, [one should perform the rite] regarding the bone-element;
likewise as before, for the four hundred thousand yoginīs and for the ten million supports.
(The ritual placement of the deities of the Śākinī retinue:
One should perform the nyāsa of Varadā, Śrī, Ṣaṇḍikā, and Sarasvatī;
the wise practitioner, having meditated upon them as before, should envision them joined with their respective seed-syllables. 260.
(The meditation on Hākinī:
She resides in the Bindu, is white in color, and holds a hand-drum, a rosary, a skull-cup, and the gesture of knowledge; she is endowed with six faces, each resplendent with three eyes.

258–259 | Having described the meditation (*dhyāna*) on Śākinī, he states the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) with the words beginning "the first letter of the alphabet" (*vādivarṇam*). Here too, as before, after *hrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ*, one recites: *vaṃ śaṃ ṣaṃ saṃ sāṃ sīṃ śa ma la va ra yūṃ śākinyai namaḥ*. Then: "O Mistress of four hundred million yoginīs residing in the bone-element of Śākinī, O Subduer of all beings, [grant] the command..."
"Dehi māṃ rakṣa rakṣa śākinīpādukāyai namaḥ"—thus one should place [this mantra] at the *mūlādhāra* as before.
By the phrase "as before," the inclusion of the remaining portions is indicated.
(260) Now, he describes the placement of her attendant deities (*parivāradevatā*) with the words beginning with "Varadā": [the mantra] is joined with the consonant *va*.

The connection is that one should install the four [goddesses] beginning with Varadā in the *mūlādhāra* lotus as previously described. Thus, the sequence of application is in the form: *vaṃ varadāyai namaḥ*, *śaṃ śriye namaḥ*, and so forth.
(p. 297) [One should contemplate her] as being attached to turmeric-colored food, delighted by the intoxication of honey, and having the nature of white marrow.
One should meditate upon that pure Goddess, who is delighted by bowing to the ocean of jewels that is the Lord of Devas. || 261 ||
(The Nyāsa of Hākinī):
The wise [practitioner] should extract *haṃ*, *kṣaṃ*, *hāṃ*, *hīṃ*, and *ca*, as well as *ha*, *ma*, *la*, *va*, *ra*, and *yuñ*.
Having uttered "Hākinīm" joined with the dative suffix *-ṅe*, the wise one should then utter the word "namḥ". (262)
And in the marrow-element itself, there are two hundred thousand koṭis of yoginīs;
after that, the word "Svāminī," and then [the words] "all beings" and so forth. (263)

(The ritual placement of the retinue: The practitioner should place [the mantras] as before, in sequence with the syllables *ha* and *kṣa*, while visualizing Sarasvatī and Kṣamā just like Hākinī. (264)
261. Regarding "located at the *bindu*": the meaning is that one should meditate [on it] in the center of the brows, in the two-petalled *ājñācakra*.

262–263. Now he states the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) with the words beginning "Haṃ Kṣam," etc. Accordingly, here too, as before, after any one of the [syllables] such as Hrīṃ Klīṃ Śrīṃ, [one recites]: "Haṃ Kṣaṃ Hāṃ Hīṃ Ha Ma La Va Ra Yūṃ, obeisance to Hākinī."

And thus, the result is that one should place [the mantra] at the *ājñā-cakra* with the words: "O Hākinī, who has entered the marrow-element (*majjā-dhātu*), sovereign of two hundred thousand million yoginīs, subduer of all beings, grant your command! Protect me, protect me! Homage to the sandals of Hākinī! (264).
Now, he describes the placement of the deities of her retinue with the verse beginning "By means of *ha* and *kṣa*," etc.; likewise, "Haṃ, to Sarasvatī."

One should place *namaḥ* and *kṣaṃ kṣamāyai namaḥ* upon the two petals in the middle of the eyebrows, while visualizing [her] like Hākinī. By this, it should be inferred that the Yoginīs belonging to the retinues of those respective deities also possess the form of their respective principal Yoginīs.
Here, this is to be noted: from the Viśuddha-cakra onwards, following the sequence down to the Mūlādhāra, up to the Ājñā-cakra.

By means of the arrangement of the letters of the Mātṛkā alphabet from *a* to *kṣ*, corresponding to the dimensions of the petals of each respective wheel (*cakra*), there is the placement (*nyāsa*) of the principal Yoginīs, such as Ḍākinī and the others, preceded by the Mātṛkā letters equal in number to the petals. In each of those lotuses, however, for the attendant Yoginīs who are equal in number to the petals, the placement is preceded by one letter per petal. Previously...

In the sixth chapter, by the passage beginning with "the goddess known as Ḍākinī shall dwell here," the locations such as the *mūlādhāra* and others for Ḍākinī and the rest have been described. However, it should be noted by the wise that there is a difference in the sequence during the ritual placement (*nyāsa*). (p. 298) [This is another system regarding the *yoginī-nyāsa*.]
Now there is another method [for the practice] consisting of the nectar of the Kula:
Brāhmī, Māheśvarī, Kaumārī, and likewise Vaiṣṇavī. || 265 ||
Vārāhī, Indrāṇī, and Cāmuṇḍā shall be the seventh; Mahālakṣmī is the eighth. These are declared in sequence as the first eight members of the group.
(These are the limbs suitable for this ritual placement: One should place these in sequence upon the head, face, throat, heart, navel, as well as the penis, anus, and feet.
The Yoginī-nyāsa has been taught; it is the destroyer of all sins. || 267 ||
(Instruction on the performance of the deposition of the zodiac signs [5]) Thereafter, one should perform the deposition of the zodiac signs, which always provides complete protection. 268.

One should contemplate them as red, white, turmeric-yellow, pale, variegated, black, tawny, reddish-brown,
dark brown, white, and smoke-colored.
265–266 | Now, beginning with the words "atha" (now) and so forth, he commences the demonstration of another sequence for the *yoginī*-installation (*nyāsa*) according to the *Kulāmṛta*:

"brāhmī" and so on. In this ritual procedure (*kalpa*), one should first install the eight groups [of letters] in order for the eight *yoginīs* beginning with Brāhmī and ending with Mahālakṣmī, as will be stated hereafter.
The Connection.

267. He states the limbs suitable for this nyāsa with the words beginning with "the head" (*śira*). The meaning is that one should sequentially install these Yoginīs, Brāhmī and the others, upon the limbs ending with the feet, starting from the head. And thus: *aṃ āṃ iṃ īṃ uṃ ūṃ ṛṃ*...

The sequence of ritual placement (*nyāsakrama*) culminates as follows: "Ṛṃ Ḷṃ Ḹṃ Eṃ Aiṃ Oṃ Auṃ Aṃ Aḥ, salutation to Brāhmī" on the head; "Kaṃ Khaṃ Gaṃ Ghaṃ Ṅaṃ, salutation to Māheśvarī" on the face, and so forth. He concludes with the verse beginning "yoginī... (verse 268). He introduces the ritual placement of the zodiac signs (*rāśinyāsa*) with the verse beginning "rāśi... (verse 269). The word "tataḥ" (then) refers to the period immediately following the aforementioned ritual placement of the Yoginīs.
269. He states the distinctions of color for the zodiac signs beginning with Aries, starting with the words "rakta" and so forth.
Thus, Aries is red and Taurus is white; in this manner, the distinctions of color for the signs beginning with Aries are to be understood in sequence.
(The procedure for ritual placement).
One should place Aries on the right ankle with the four letters beginning with 'A'; Taurus on the knee with two [letters]; and Gemini on the shank with four [letters]. (270)
With two [bindus] on the belly, one should place Cancer; with a pair on the shoulder, Leo;
and with the bindu, the sarga-visarga, and the śa-group of consonants on the right head, Virgo.
The left side [of the body] is [assigned] with the *ka*-group, and then the sign called Libra;
Scorpio with the *ca*-group; likewise, Sagittarius on the shoulders and the flanks with the *ṭa*-group and so forth. (272)

270 | He shows the sequence of the *nyāsa* with the words beginning "akāra" and so forth. Here too, as before, the application of any one of the seed-syllables such as *hrīṃ*, *klīṃ*, or *śrīṃ* should be inferred as previously described. And thus, on the right ankle:
(1) *hrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ aṃ āṃ iṃ īṃ namaḥ to the Aries zodiac sign*.
(2) Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Aṃ Āṃ Iṃ Īṃ, salutation to the Aries zodiac sign. (3) Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Aṃ Āṃ Iṃ Īṃ, salutation to the Aries zodiac sign; Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ.
(4) Klīṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Aṃ Āṃ Iṃ Īṃ, salutation to the Aries zodiac sign.
Thus, one of these various methods of ritual placement (*nyāsa*) is to be understood. The same should be known for Taurus (*vṛṣa*) and the other signs as follows:
having uttered any one of these [vowels], one should say *uṃ ūṃ vṛṣarāśaye namaḥ* at the right knee; and *ṛṃ ṝṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ mithunarāśaye namaḥ* at the right testicle.

"By two" means *eṃ aiṃ*; "salutation to the zodiac sign Cancer" is on the right side of the abdomen. *Oṃ auṃ salutation to the zodiac sign Leo* is on the right shoulder. Regarding "the bindu": the bindu is the anusvāra; the sarga is the visarga;
the *śa*-group consists of the six letters *śa ṣa sa ha la kṣa*. Thus, *aṃ aḥ śaṃ ṣaṃ saṃ haṃ laṃ kṣaṃ* [is for] the zodiac sign Virgo.
"Namaḥ" [is placed] on the right head; that is to say, on the right side of the head.

272. "On the left head": thus, *kaṃ khaṃ gaṃ ghaṃ ṅaṃ tulārāśaye namaḥ* (Salutation to the sign of Libra) is on the left head. "By means of the *ca*-group": *caṃ chaṃ jaṃ jhaṃ ñaṃ vṛścikarāśaye namaḥ* (Salutation to the sign of Scorpio) is on the left shoulder.

Regarding the phrase "with the [consonants] beginning with ṭa": the meaning is that one should perform the placement on the left side of the abdomen with the mantra *ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ ḍhaṃ ṇaṃ dhanūrāśaye namaḥ*.

Then, one should place Capricorn (*makara*) upon the testicles with the *ṭa*-group (*tavarga*), and likewise, one should place Aquarius (*kumbha*) upon the left knee with the *pa*-group (*pavarga*). (p. 500)
The *y*-group, along with its corresponding vowels, is located in the left ankle, known as Mīna.
(Another sequence for describing the colors of the zodiac signs:
These—Sagittarius, Cancer, Gemini, and Virgo—are yellow in both [the male and female forms].
Libra, Capricorn, Aries, and Cancer possess a red luster.
The remaining four mobile [elements] and the four stable ones are considered separately as white. || 275 ||
(Regarding the determination of the places for nyāsa, there is a difference in sequence:
On the right foot, likewise on the *liṅga*, on the right side of the belly, and in the heart;
on the right hand, on the right side of the head, and likewise on the left. 276.
One should likewise place [the mantras] on the head, on the left side, on the left arm, in the heart,
in the left belly, on the penis, and on the left foot.
273. Regarding "makara": *taṃ thaṃ daṃ dhaṃ naṃ makararāśaye namaḥ*—thus on the left testicle.
Regarding "with the *pa*-group": *paṃ phaṃ baṃ bhaṃ maṃ kumbharāśaye namaḥ*—thus on the left knee.
274. Regarding "and the *ya*-group": here, in the fourteenth chapter of the *Jñānārṇava* and the ninth chapter of the *Gandharvatantra*—
"By the *ya*-group and the letter *kṣa*, [one places] Pisces on the left ankle.
From this statement, it is understood that one should perform the placement (*nyāsa*) on the left ankle with the mantra: *yaṃ raṃ laṃ vaṃ kṣaṃ mīnarāśaye namaḥ*.
In the *Tantrasāra*, only the application of the Mātṛkā letters *yaṃ raṃ laṃ vaṃ* is seen. Here, the *ya*-group [is used] along with its corresponding vowel.
It appears that these two lines beginning with "cavargacaramārṇaiḥ" are merely due to a scribal error.

(275) Demonstrating an alternative method for the classification of the signs (*rāśi*) by letters and their positions in the diagram, he first states the classification of letters starting with the verse beginning "cāpa... (the bow).

276–277 | Regarding "the right foot": in this ritual manual (*kalpa*), having combined the seed-syllables (*bīja*) and the groups (*varga*) according to the sequence previously described, one should place Aries on the right foot, Taurus on the right side of the *liṅga*, Gemini on the right abdomen, and Cancer on the right side of the heart.
(The Installation of the Seats [6])
Thereafter, one should arrange the seats which consist of all ritual actions.
(Regarding the determination of the colors of those seats: White, reddish-brown, dark, green, and yellow are their incomparable colors in sequence. (278)
Again and again, in due order, the practitioner of mantra should meditate upon the collection of the fifty seats for the sake of attaining all desired goals and purposes. (279)
(The names of the seats: Kāmarūpa is a great seat; then there is the seat of Vārāṇasī;
Nepāla is a great seat, and Pauṇḍravardhana is indeed a seat. || 280 ||
One should place Leo on the right hand, Virgo on the right side of the head, Libra on the left side, and Scorpio on the left hand;
Sagittarius on the left shoulder of the heart, Capricorn on the left flank, Aquarius on the left side of the *liṅga*,
and Pisces on the left foot— this is the distinction from the previous [method].

278–279. Having thus described the fivefold installation beginning with Gaṇeśa, which constitutes a limb of the sixfold installation (*ṣoḍhānyāsa*), he now states the final installation, that of the sacred seats (*pīṭhanyāsa*), beginning with the words "the seats" (*pīṭhāni*). Therein, he first explains the distinctions of color for the seats, beginning with the word "white" (*sita*). The meaning is that the colors of the seats are to be determined by repeating the sequence beginning with "white and red" (*sitāruṇa*) and so forth. Regarding this, it is stated in the *Tantrasāra*:
White, black, reddish-brown, dark, green, and yellow—
in this sequence, O Goddess, there is a collection of fifty locations repeated again and again.
[One should visualize them] as dark-complexioned, with hands in the gestures of granting boons and fearlessness, adorned with all ornaments.

Thus, the meditation on the *pīṭhas* has been described. Regarding the word "anupama" in the root text, since its connection with the term "pīṭhāni" is untenable and because there is an absence of any description of a characteristic called "Anupamā," the reading "anupama" is to be considered doubtful.
(280) He states the different names of the *pīṭhas* beginning with "Kāmarūpa. Here...
