May all these yoginīs, protected and hidden, guard [the practitioner] upon the surface of the earth; having performed this pervasion, one should worship the leader, Tripureśvarī. (417)
One should install these three— the mudrā that causes all to flee, as well as the vision of Brahman— upon the liṅga according to the procedure taught by the Guru.
(The placement of the third enclosure: Then, one should perform the pervasive placement (*vyāpaka-nyāsa*) at the end of the mantra "Salutation to the eight-petaled lotus.
Thereafter, one should place the deities beginning with Anaṅgakusumā. (419)

The practitioner, having performed [the placement] starting from the left ankle in reverse order, should place them on the right cheek, above the breast, on the right thigh, and on the right ankle. (420)

According to this statement from the fourth chapter of the *Tantrarāja*, the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) should be performed as before, preceded by the two seed-syllables *hrīṃ* and *śrīṃ*, joined with each individual vowel. Thus: *hrīṃ śrīṃ aṃ kāmākarṣiṇīnityākalāyai namaḥ* on the right ear; *hrīṃ śrīṃ āṃ buddhyākarṣiṇīnityākalāyai namaḥ* on the right shoulder-blade; and so on, down to the sole of the right foot.

Having first placed [the seed-syllables] within the Gandhākarṣiṇī, one should again place the eight [deities] beginning with Cittākarṣiṇī, starting from the sole of the left foot up to the right ear. The sequence for that is as follows: "Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Ḷṃ, obeisance to the eternal digit (nityā-kalā) Cittākarṣiṇī" on the sole of the left foot; "Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Ḹṃ, obeisance to the eternal digit Dhairyākarṣiṇī" on the left ankle. In this manner, the procedure for the others should also be understood.
417–418 | “These” (etāḥ) means that all these [deities] and so forth should be installed as pervaders within the aforementioned wheel of emanation (*sṛṣṭicakra*).
“The heroine” (*nāyikām*) means the heroine of the Śrīcakra. And thus, as before, having uttered the two seed-syllables:
“Obeisance to Tripureśvarī, the heroine of the cakra; obeisance to the mudrā that subdues all; likewise, obeisance to the vision of Brahman.”

One should place these three [mantras] upon the *liṅga* according to the procedure taught by the Guru. However, in both the *Tripurārcanarahasya* and the *Pūjāprakaraṇa* of the *Tantrasāra*, it is observed that the *Cakranāyikā* is preceded by the *Bālā* seed-syllable (*bīja*), and the *Sarvavidrāviṇī-mudrā* is preceded by the *Māyā* seed-syllable. Furthermore, in the *Tantrasāra*, the reading "for the vision of Brahman" (*brahmadarśanāya*) appears as "for the vision of the Buddha" (*bauddhadarśanāya*). In the *Tripurārcanarahasya*, however, this [latter reading] is not accepted.

It has been done. And thus, because differences of opinion are seen here in various tantras, one should proceed according to the instructions of one's own respective guru; this is precisely what he states by the phrase "having reached the end of the procedure taught by the Guru" (419–420). Having thus described the method of ritual placement (*nyāsa*) upon the sixteen petals of the second enclosure (*āvaraṇa*), [he continues].

He describes the procedure for the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) within the eight-petalled lotus of the third enclosure (*tṛtīyāvaraṇa*) with the words beginning "Then" (*tataḥ*). Here too, since no specific [deities] are mentioned, [it refers to those previously stated]:
"May all these most secret [goddesses], situated in the eight-petalled [lotus] of the third enclosure—the wheel of emanation (*sṛṣṭicakra*) that causes agitation—protect [me]. (421)
Having performed this pervasion (vyāpaka) for the illustrious Tripurasundarī,
as well as for the Ākarṣiṇī Mahāmudrā and likewise for the Śaiva system,
the best of practitioners should place this nyāsa in the region of the navel. 422.
(The placement of the fourth enclosure: At the end [of the mantra], one should place "Salutation to the fourteen-spoked wheel" as the pervasive [mantra].
The practitioner should place [the mantras] beginning with "Sarvasaṃkṣobhiṇī" in its corners. 423.

As before, it should be understood that [the mantras] are preceded by the seed-syllables of Māyā and Śrī. This is because it will be stated in the section on the worship of the Cakra in the eighteenth chapter:

"The practitioner of mantra should worship on the eight petals with those ending in the consonantal groups beginning with Ka," and because the authors of the *Tripurārcanarahasya* have likewise described the application of the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) for the eight [Śaktis] beginning with Anaṅgakusumā as being preceded by the first letter of each consonantal group.

The essential point is that it must be performed. Thus, the meaning is that one should perform the placement (*nyāsa*) by way of pervasion (*vyāpaka*), reciting: *hrīṃ śrīṃ aṣṭadalapadmāya namaḥ*. In the *Tripurārcanarahasya* as well, it is stated: "Then, having pervaded the locations starting from Anaṅgakusumā and so forth, [one should say] 'salutation to the wheel of the eight-petaled lotus' (*aṣṭadalapadmacakrāya namaḥ*). Regarding "Anaṅga": then, in the four locations beginning with the right cheek and ending with the right ankle, [one should proceed] in reverse order.
The connection is as follows: one should sequentially assign the eight [deities] beginning with Anaṅgakusumā to the four locations starting from the left ankle and ending at the left cheek.
These, beginning with Anaṅgakusumā, are:
Anaṅgakusumā, Anaṅgamekhalā, Anaṅgamadanā, Anaṅgamadanāturā, Anaṅgarekhā, Anaṅgaveginī, and Anaṅgāṅkuśā.

The internal impurities [are as follows]. The means of valid cognition (*pramāṇa*) and so forth will be explained in the eighteenth [chapter]. Thus, one should perform the placement starting with *hrīṃ śrīṃ kaṃ anaṅgakusumāyai namaḥ* on the right cheek; continuing in this sequence down to the right ankle, and then again in reverse order, starting with *hrīṃ śrīṃ paṃ anaṅgarekhāyai namaḥ* from the left ankle up to the left cheek.
The result is that one should place [the deities] ending with Anaṅgamālinī; the remainder is easy to understand.

(422) "By this" means by the sequence beginning with the third enclosure (*tṛtīyāvaraṇa*). However, in the *Tripurārcanarahasya*, it is stated: "One should place these four—the Guptatarayoginīs together with their mudrās—in the heart, within the wheel of universal agitation (*sarvasaṃkṣobhaṇa*). [Regarding the word] "Śrīmat":

The result is that one should perform the placement (*nyāsa*) at the region of the navel with the words: "Salutation to the illustrious Tripurasundarī, salutation to the All-Attracting One, salutation to the Śaiva Vision.
(423–425) Now, he describes the procedure for the fourteen-spoked wheel within the eight-petaled lotus, beginning with the verse starting "fourteen," etc.

Here too, as before, one should perform the placement by joining the letters from *ka* to *ḍha*, preceded by the seed-syllable of Māyāśrī. Likewise, on the fourteen-spoked [cakra], one should place them on the right side of the forehead, the cheeks, the shoulders, and the back.
One should place [the mantras] on the sides, the thighs, and the shanks with a clockwise rotation. || 424 ||
In these regions, the sequence [of mantras] on the back and behind is in reverse order;
may those who belong to the true tradition protect [us] in the fourteenth corner of the wheel.
Having performed this pervasion, the wise one should place the Vaśyamudrā and likewise the visualization of the Sun within the heart of the Goddess residing in Tripura.

The meaning is as follows: having pervaded [the body] with "cakrāya," one should assign the seven [deities] beginning with Sarvasaṃkṣobhiṇī to the seven locations starting from the right side of the forehead and ending with the right calf; then, again in reverse order, having assigned them to the locations starting from the left calf and ending with the left side of the forehead—excluding the back—one should finally assign the last Yoginī to the back at the very end of all [locations].
In the third chapter of the *Yoginīhṛdaya*, however, it is said: "O Pārvatī, [the sequence begins] with the forehead, then the right side, the middle of the right cheek and shoulder,
the other side [the left], the thighs, the interior of the shanks, and so on, beginning with the left shank."
The end of the left thigh, the left side, the left shoulder, the left cheek,
the middle of the forehead on the left, and likewise the back.

In this statement, without specifying a placement on the right shoulder (*dakṣapṛṣṭha*), seven locations are mentioned for the right side by distinguishing between the forehead and the right portion of the forehead. However, it should be noted that the intention of Pūrṇānanda appears to be that because of the mention of the "right shoulder" (*dakṣapṛṣṭha*) here, the placement is specifically on the right part of the forehead and not even in the middle of the forehead. In this context, the word "shoulder" (*pṛṣṭha*)...
It indicates the back of the head. As it was stated by Amṛtānandanātha in his commentary on the *Yoginīhṛdaya*: "The term 'back' (pṛṣṭha) should be understood as the back of the head.
Furthermore, [the mudrās] beginning with Sarvasaṃkṣobhiṇī are: Sarvasaṃkṣobhiṇī, Sarvavidrāviṇī, Sarvākarṣiṇī, Sarvāhlādinī, ...

The fourteen [powers] are: the deluder of all, the paralyzer of all, the yawner of all, the subjugator of all, the delighter of all, the intoxicater of all, the accomplisher of all aims, the fulfiller of all prosperity, the embodiment of all mantras, and the destroyer of all dualities.
The specific details should be seen in the eighteenth [chapter].

And thus, having performed the placement (*nyāsa*) in this sequence— first *hrīṃ śrīṃ kaṃ sarvasaṃkṣobhiṇīśaktyai namaḥ* on the right forehead, and *hrīṃ śrīṃ khaṃ sarvavidrāviṇyai namaḥ* on the right cheek— one should then place [the remaining syllables] starting from the left calf in the order beginning with *hrīṃ śrīṃ jaṃ sarvavaśaṅkaryai namaḥ*, ending at the right side of the forehead; this is the established conclusion.
425–426 | Next, he states what is to be done, beginning with the word "cakra": "And thus, upon the cakra—
(the placement of the fifth enclosure)— one should perform the pervasive [placement] at the end of 'namo bahirdaśāracakrāya'."
In the right eye, at the root of the right nostril, and in the lower right eye. || 427 ||
One should also place [the deities] in the pair of knees at the northwest corner and in the secret region;
and one should place the deity Sarvasiddhi and the others in the left side of the belly and in the southwest (Nirṛti).

The meaning is that, having performed the placement (nyāsa) by way of pervasion with the mantra beginning "samparadāyinya," one should first place Tripurāvāsinī, the Mistress of the Wheel (cakreśvarī), in the heart; then the Vaśyamudrā; and then the Sūryadarśana.
In the Śrīyantra, there are two wheels within the fourteen-spoked wheel, namely the ten-cornered [wheel] and the [inner] wheel.

It should be understood that the ten-spoked wheel situated outside those two is the "outer ten-spoked" (*bahir-daśāra*), and that which is situated within them is the "inner ten-spoked" (*antar-daśāra*). Regarding this, he describes the procedure for the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) in the first [wheel], the outer ten-spoked wheel called *Sarvārthasādhaka*, beginning with the words "outside," and so forth.

Here too, as will be stated in the sequence of worship (*pūjākrama*), one should provide the letters beginning with *ṇa* and ending with *bha* after the seed-syllables of Māyā and Śrī, just as before.

Having joined each letter individually, beginning with *ṇa* and ending with *bha*, one should install the Yoginīs of the Ten Families of Kaula who bestow all accomplishments (*sarvasiddhipradā*). Regarding the locations for this installation, he says "the right eye" (*dakṣākṣī*) and so forth. On this point, Amṛtānandanātha states in his commentary on the *Yoginīhṛdaya*:
"Starting from the two arms and extending to the two thighs, the region is indicated by the term 'belly' (*kukṣi*); therefore, the upper portion of the belly is the East."

The lower part consists of the western and the right and left sides, which are the southern and northern directions respectively. By the word "corner" (*koṇa*), the arms and thighs are understood. Thus, the base of the left arm is the northeast corner (*īśakoṇa*), the base of the left thigh is the northwest corner (*vāyukoṇa*), the base of the right thigh is the southwest corner (*nairṛtakoṇa*), and the base of the right arm is the southeast corner (*agnikoṇa*). In this manner, here the term "northwest corner" refers to the base of the left thigh, and the term "southwest" refers to...

It is understood as the root of the right thigh. Thus, [the sequence is]: in the right eye, at the base of the nose, in the left eye, then on the right side of the abdomen (meaning the right flank), then on the root of the left thigh, the right knee, the left knee, the secret region, the left flank, and the root of the right thigh. The essential meaning is that one should sequentially install the deities, beginning with Sarvasiddhi, in these ten locations.

And [the goddesses] beginning with Sarvasiddhi—namely Sarvasiddhipradā, Sarvasampatpradā, Sarvapriyaṅkarī, Sarvamaṅgalakāriṇī, Sarvakāmapradā, Sarvaduḥkhamocinī, Sarvamṛtyupraśamanī, Sarvavighnavināśinī, Sarvāṅgasundarī, and Sarvasaubhāgyadāyinī—are those to be described in the eighteenth chapter. And thus: Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Ṇaṃ.

"Obeisance to the Bestower of All Siddhis," thus [one should place it] on the right eye; "Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Taṃ, obeisance to the Bestower of All Wealth," thus on the root of the nose. In this manner, one should perform the placement (*nyāsa*) in sequence upon the other aforementioned limbs. This is the established conclusion. [They] reside in the fifth enclosure within the wheel that accomplishes all aims (*sarvārthasādhaka*).
The Kulayoginīs have made me their own; may the ten deities protect me. 429.
Having performed this as a pervasive rite, one should then [worship] Tripurāśrī,
Unmādinī, and Vaiṣṇavī at the pit of the throat (galakūpaka).
(6. The Assignment of the Sixty Arrows: One should perform the pervasive assignment at the end with "Obeisance to the Inner Wheel of Ten Arrows" (*antardaśaracakrāya namaḥ*).
Then, the mantra-practitioner, being composed, should assign the [deities] beginning with Sarvajña to these [locations]. (431)
Then, on the nose, the corners of the mouth, the palms, the testicles, and the anus;
thereafter, following the same leftward sequence, one should place [the hand] on the testicle and the breast.

429–430 | Next, he states what is to be done with the verse beginning "sarvārtha" and so forth. Thus, having performed the placement [of the mantra] as a pervasive [layer] starting with "sarvārtha," one should place Tripurāśrī, the Mistress of the Cakra, as well as Unmādinī and the Vaiṣṇava weapon in the hollow of the throat; this is the meaning. This concludes the placement of the fifth enclosure.
431. Having thus explained the placement (*nyāsa*) of the outer ten-spoked wheel, he states the sequence for the placement of the inner ten-spoked wheel with the words beginning "inside" (*antaḥ*).

Here too, as before, the conjunction of the *māyā* and *śrī* seed-syllables must be performed. Thus, the meaning is that one should perform the placement by pervading the ten corners with the mantra: *hrīṃ śrīṃ antardaśaracakrāya namaḥ*. Then, the practitioner...
One who knows the secret of the mantra, being composed, should install the ten [deities] beginning with Sarvajñā in these locations to be described hereafter.

The ten beginning with Sarvajñā are: Sarvajñā (the All-knowing), Sarvaśakti (All-powerful), Sarveśvaryapradāyinī (Bestower of all sovereignty), Sarvajñānamayī (Consisting of all knowledge), Sarvavyādhivināśinī (Destroyer of all diseases), Sarvādhārasvarūpā (The nature of the support of all), Sarvapāpaharā (Remover of all sins), Sarvānandamayī (Consisting of all bliss), Sarvarakṣāsvarūpiṇī (The nature of the protection of all), and Sarvepsitaphalapradā (Bestower of the fruits of all desires).

These will be explained [below]. 432. It was stated that one should place [the mantras] upon these while being composed (*samāhita*); he now defines those locations for placement (*nyāsasthāna*) with the words beginning "on the nose" (*nāsāyām*). Regarding the phrase "precisely by the leftward sequence": first, [one places] Sarvajñā and the others on the locations starting from the nose and ending at the anus.

Having placed the five [mantras] ending with *sarvavyādhivināśinī* according to the sequence of the right side, one should then place the five [mantras] beginning with *sarvādhārasvarūpā* and ending with *sarvepsitaphalapradā* on the left side, starting from the testicle and ending at the eye; this is the established conclusion. However, in the third chapter of the *Yoginīhṛdaya*:
May those [deities], situated in the source of all protection, protect us at the corners of the mouth, the nose, and the eyes; may they protect us within the ten corners. 433.
The Nigarbha-yoginīs are established in the sixth enclosure;
having performed the pervasive [placement] with this, as well as with Tripuramālinī, [one should proceed]. (434)
The supreme practitioner should place these three—the Great Hook, the Great Seal, and the Vision of the Victor—between the eyebrows. 435.
(The placement of the seventh enclosure:
Next, one should perform the pervasive placement ending with "namas" for the eight-spoked wheel;
one should then place the eight goddesses of speech, beginning with Vaśinī, in these locations. 436.
The right nostril, the corner of the mouth, the breast, and the testicle;
the left testicle, the breast, the corner of the mouth, the two nostrils,
and the tip of the nose— this is to be known as the ten corners (koṇas).
By this [statement], without treating the placement (*nyāsa*) on the eyes as a limb of the *nirukta-nyāsa*, the placement on the tip of the nose (*nāsāgra*) is prescribed there.

The same is the case in the *Tripurārcanarahasya*. Thus, it should be understood that here there exists a difference in the sequence of the placement (*nyāsa*) due to the differences between the various traditions (*āgama*). Since it will be stated in the eighteenth chapter (*prakāśa*) that "one should worship with the letters from *ma* to *kṣa*," [the sequence] follows after the *māyā-bīja* and *śrī-bīja*.

It should be understood that the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) is to be performed by joining each letter individually from *ma* to *kṣa*. Thus, one should perform the placement as follows: *hrīṃ śrīṃ gaṃ sarvajñāyai namaḥ* on the right nostril; *hrīṃ śrīṃ yaṃ sarvaśaktyai namaḥ* on the left nostril.
In this same sequence, the placement should also be performed on the corners of the mouth and other locations. Then, *hrīṃ śrīṃ śaṃ*...

It should be understood that one should perform the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) in the sequence beginning with "Salutation to her whose nature is the support of all" upon the left testicle and other parts [of the body].

(433–435) "May they protect us," and so forth. Then, having pervaded [the body] starting from "May they protect us in the ten corners," one should first worship Tripurāmālinī, the Mistress of the Wheel (*cakreśvarī*), according to the previously mentioned sequence; thereafter, one should worship Mahāṅkuśā, Mahāmudrā, and the Jina-doctrine (*jinadarśana*).

"One should place [the mantra] between the eyebrows"—this is the placement for the sixth enclosure (ṣaṣṭhāvaraṇanyāsa). 436–437. Now, he describes the placement of the eight-spoked wheel (*aṣṭāracakra*) within the previously mentioned inner ten-spoked wheel (*antardaśāracakra*), beginning with the word "atha" (now). Thus, having performed the pervasive placement (*vyāpakatvena vinyasya*) with the mantra "Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, obeisance to the eight-spoked wheel," one should [place] the eight goddesses of speech, Vaśinī and the others, upon these [spokes].
At the chin, the right throat, the heart, and the region of the navel—
in these locations, one should proceed in reverse order on the left side according to this rite.
May these secret yoginīs always protect [me] in the eight corners;
having performed this pervasive [protection], [one honors] Tripurā, the sole mistress of accomplishments. (438)
Furthermore, the foremost of practitioners should place these three— the Great Seal (mahāmudrā) known as Khecarī, as well as the Vision of Power (śaktidarśana)— upon the forehead.
(The ritual placement for the eighth enclosure:

Then, one should perform the pervasive placement ending with "namas" for the three-pointed wheel, in the four directions outside the triangle situated at the heart, proceeding from the exterior. (440)
Then [he holds] the five arrows beginning with Jambhana, the bow of Mohana, the noose of Vaśīkaraṇa, and the goad of Stambhana. (441)
The connection is that one should "place" [the mantras] in the locations to be described hereafter. He states those locations with the words beginning with "chin" (*cibuka*).

"By this rite" means by the procedure taught in the sequence for the placement (*nyāsa*) of Vaśinī and the others. First, having placed the group of four beginning with Vaśinī on the right side in the four internal locations starting from the chin and ending at the navel, one then proceeds in reverse order to the left shoulder, starting from the navel and ending at the chin.

One should perform the placement (*vinyāsa*) of the four [deities] beginning with Aruṇā. This placement should be performed preceded by the two seed-syllables *hrīṃ* and *śrīṃ*, strictly according to the previously mentioned sequence of the placement of Vaśinī and the others; therefore, there is no need for a detailed demonstration here.
Only a mere indication of its direction is shown: *hrīṃ śrīṃ*, followed by from *aṃ* up to *aḥ*, and then *blūṃ*.
"Salutation to Vaśinī Vāgdevatā" on the left chin; in this manner, it should be inferred for other locations as well.

(438–349) Next, he states what is to be done with the words beginning with "etā" (these): having thus performed the placement (*nyāsa*) by way of pervasion, starting with the secret yoginīs and so forth, preceded by the aforementioned seed-syllables, one offers salutation to Tripurāsiddhā Cakreśvarī and to Khecarīmudrā.
The result is that one should place these three—*namaḥ*, *śaktidarśanāya*, and *namaḥ*—on the forehead. This concludes the placement (*nyāsa*) of the seventh enclosure.

[440-441] Now, he demonstrates the placement of the triangular wheel (*tryasracakra*) within the eight-spoked wheel (*aṣṭāracakra*), beginning with the words "Then," and so forth. Here too, as before, the application of the seed-syllables (*bījayoga*) should be understood. Thus, one performs the pervasive placement (*vyāpakanyāsa*) with the mantra: *tryasrāya cakrāya namaḥ*.
The six-limbed maiden, in the form of the limbs, should be placed upon them;
Kāmapīṭha is in the front corner, and Jālandhara is on the right. (442)
Likewise, Pūrṇapīṭha is in the left [corner], which is designated as Fire, Sun, and Moon;
and in the three corners, one should worship Kāmeśī, Vajreśī, and Bhagamālinī.
These are the supreme, most secret Yoginīs who bestow all accomplishments;
one should extract the word in the station of the triangular abode within the Cakra.
"May the Śrī-devīs be worshipped; one should install them by means of pervasion. (444)
The mantra-practitioner should sequentially place Tripurāmbikā, Cakreśī, Mudrā, and likewise Bījābhidhā, as well as the Śākta-darśana, upon the forehead.
(The placement of the ninth enclosure: Then, one should perform the pervasive placement (*vyāpaka-nyāsa*) at the end with "Salutation to the Baindava-cakra.
Thereafter, [one should worship] the venerable Tripurasundarī, whose form is Brahman. 446.

The meaning is that one should place [the mantras]. In the *Tripurārcanarahasya*, however, the formula "Obeisance to the triangle-wheel with its intermediate spaces" (*sāntarālatrikoṇacakrāya namaḥ*) is observed.
He describes the sequence of placement (*nyāsa*), preceded by the determination of the locations, beginning with the words "situated in the heart," and so forth.
[This refers to] the triangle situated within the pericarp of the lotus of the heart known as Anāhata, [with mantras to be placed] in the four directions outside it in due order.

The connection is that one should install the five arrows beginning with Jambhana, the Sammohana bow, the Vaśīkaraṇa noose, and the Stambhana goad. Regarding this, it is said in the sixteenth chapter of the *Jñānārṇava*:
"Having uttered the five arrows consisting of Kāma and Kāmeśvarī..."
O Great Goddess, one should worship the deity Bāṇa, known as Jambhana.

Because of this statement, it should be understood that the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) must be performed with the arrows of Kāmeśvara and the arrows of Kāmeśvarī. For this very reason, in the *Tripurārcanarahasya*, the venerable Brahmānanda has demonstrated the sequence of practice in such a form as: "Oṃ drāṃ drīṃ blūṃ saḥ yāṃ rāṃ lāṃ vāṃ śāṃ, obeisance to the arrows of Kāmeśvara and Kāmeśvarī for the purpose of paralyzing (*jambhana*)," and so forth.

The sequence of placement (*nyāsa*) preceded by the *pañcabāṇa* mantra has been specifically demonstrated on the occasion of the placement of the weapons (*āyudhanyāsa*), and thus is not repeated here. The remainder is clear.
(446–448) Now, he describes the arrangement for the placement of the *bindu-cakra*, which consists of universal bliss, within the triangle: *tataḥ*...
In the triangle known as the Eye, within the wheel consisting of all bliss, may the venerable goddesses who abide in the supreme and non-supreme secret be worshipped. 447.
Having performed this pervasion, one should install Bhairavī, the Mistress of the Wheel, [upon] the head, throat, mouth, ears, eyes, nose, and the two arms. (448)
The heart, the secret place, likewise the back, the navel, and then the belly;
the secret place, the foot, and the ankle—this is the fifteen-syllable [mantra] of the Goddess. (449)
Having thus cast off the body, one should cast off speech into the fifth [element];
having uttered the five peaks (pañcakūṭa), one should [merge] the fifth [vowel], Tripureśvarī.
Likewise, the Saubhāgyā, the Lopāmudrā, and the twenty-five-syllable mantra,
according to the divisions of the six Āmnāyas, whether pertaining to Śakti or to Śambhu.

By such [statements] as these, because it is presided over by the venerable Tripurasundarī in the form of the supreme *bindu*, it possesses the nature of the *baindava-cakra*. Thus, having performed the placement (*nyāsa*) pervasively with "Obeisance to the *baindava-cakra*," and having placed the venerable Tripurasundarī within the wheel consisting of universal bliss (*sarvānandamaya-cakra*), one should then perform the placement pervasively with "O Śrī Devī," and so forth; this is the established conclusion. Regarding the term "the Mistress of the Wheel" (*cakreśī*): [it refers to] Tripurabhairavī, the Sovereign of the Wheel.

The meaning is that one should perform the placement (*nyāsa*) with "namaḥ" in the *nirukta*-cakra. However, in the *Tripurārcanarahasya*, a sequence is observed wherein, after "namaḥ to the Baindava-cakra," one performs the placement with "namaḥ to Śrī Mahātripurasundarī" preceded by the root mantra; then, having uttered the root mantra, one should perform the placement with "namaḥ to Tripurabhairavī Cakreśvarī," and so forth. Regarding "the head": [this refers to] the goddess Śrī Tripurasundarī.
The meaning is that one should perform the placement (*nyāsa*) of each individual syllable of the fifteen-syllable mantra upon the fifteen locations, beginning with the head.

[Verses 450–451] "The five peaks" (*pañcakūṭa*) means that which was previously demonstrated. One should perform the placement of either Tripureśvarī—who consists of twenty-five syllables and is composed of five peaks—or Saubhāgyā (Lopāmudrā), who is composed of three peaks.

The connection [is as follows]. Regarding the phrase "according to the sixfold tradition" (*ṣaḍāmnāya*): the meaning is that this ritual placement (*nyāsa*) should be performed with the twenty-five-syllable Vidyā among those various Vidyās previously demonstrated according to the divisions of the sixfold tradition and the divisions of the Śākta and Śāmbhava traditions.
(p. 541) One should place Gaṇapati on the region of the head and Vaṭuka on the two ears.
One should place Kṣetrapāla in the heart and Yoginī in the anus.
One should place Nirmālyavāsinī on the face, and Śeṣikā at the Bindu;
one should place Yonimudrā on the region of the head and Parāśakti as well.
(Conclusion of the Śrīcakra-nyāsa) The Śrīcakra-nyāsa has been taught; it is exceedingly difficult to obtain even in the three worlds.
(The secret nature of this nyāsa)
It must not be given to anyone whatsoever; it must never be given. || 454 ||
(The Pervasive Deposition):
Having performed the pervasive deposition (*vyāpakanyāsa*) fivefold, sevenfold, or even ninefold with the root mantra, the practitioner himself becomes the venerable Tripurā. (455)
Thus ends the fifteenth chapter in the *Śrītattvacintāmaṇi* composed by the venerable Pūrṇānanda Paramahaṃsa. || 15 ||
452–453 | Next, he teaches the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) of Gaṇapati and the others upon the crown of the head and other parts, beginning with the words "Gaṇapatim" and so forth.
This is clear.
